rows.original:
More ruins mark the site of some battle that'd happened in the long-forgotten past — the burnt-out remains of these buildings are done up in imperial Belharan rather than Minoan architecture, and great rents and gouges have been clawed into the rocky mountainside, distinctly artificial against the Windy Peaks' natural ruggedness. Time doesn't seem to have healed these wounds, and the cold dry has only served to preserve these remains as opposed to grinding them down...

        One can guess at what happened: without the ability to retreat into the mountain and no easy way down it, whatever imperials were stationed here decided to make some kind of stand regardless of the odds lined up against them. Given that the scorched remains look more like some kind of luxury housing rather than anything that's fortifiable, one can surmise that it didn't go well for them. A heavy, oppressive aura hangs about these ruins even though the winds continually whip through the blasted shell that once held life — best to move on if there's nothing you're seeking here in particular.
rows.translation:
更多的废墟标志着很久以前发生过的一场战役的遗址——这些被烧毁的建筑残骸采用了贝拉兰帝国的建筑风格，而非米诺斯风格；在岩石山坡上，人们开凿出了巨大的沟壑和凹槽，这些人工痕迹与风啸峰的自然崎岖地貌形成了鲜明的对比。时间似乎并未治愈这些伤痕，寒冷干燥的环境反而让这些遗迹得以保存下来，而非被侵蚀殆尽……

        人们可以猜测当时发生了什么：由于无法退回到山中，也没有便捷的下山路径，驻扎在这里的帝国军队决定不顾一切地坚守下去，哪怕胜算微乎其微。从这些烧焦的残骸来看，它们更像是一些豪华住宅，而非可以用于防御的设施，因此可以推测，他们遭遇的结局肯定不妙。尽管风不断吹拂着这片曾经充满生机的废墟，但这里依然弥漫着一种重型、压抑的气氛。如果你在这里并没有特别想要寻找的东西，那么最好还是离开吧。

"

Time doesn't seem to have healed these wounds, and the cold dry has only served to preserve these remains as opposed to grinding them down...

        One can guess at what happened: without the ability to retreat into the mountain and no easy way down it, whatever imperials were stationed here decided to make some kind of stand regardless of the odds lined up against them. Given that the scorched remains look more like some kind of luxury housing rather than anything that's fortifiable, one can surmise that it didn't go well for them. A heavy, oppressive aura hangs about these ruins even though the winds continually whip through the blasted shell that once held life — best to move on if there's nothing you're seeking here in particular."

rows.original: Another set of stairs that lead into the Undermountain much like the one you emerged from, only this time blocked by rubble. Looks like the minotaurs once had more to do on the exterior of their mountain home, but have retreated into the tunnels of late. Presumably there're more exits like these all around the mountain... how many are still usable, let alone in use? The numerous ruins that dot the slopes imply that they weren't always as thick with harpies as they are today... although you can see why even the mighty minotaurs are reluctant to take on the feathered horde roosting atop their home.
rows.translation: 另一组通往地下山的楼梯，与你当初出来的那组楼梯非常相似，只不过这次被废墟堵住了。看来那些弥诺陶洛斯曾经在他们的山体外面还有许多事情要处理，但最近已经退回到了隧道里去了。大概在整个山上，还有许多这样的出口……其中还有多少是能够使用的，更别提真正有人在用了呢？那些散布在山坡上的众多废墟说明，过去这里并不像现在这样到处都是鹰身女妖。…尽管你可以理解，为什么就连强大的弥诺陶洛斯们也不愿意去对付那些栖息在他们家园上空的羽毛族群。

rows.original:
The dry air suddenly turns into a freezing mist as you continue along the mountain trail, and with a shivering start you realize the reason for the sudden change: you're walking through a cloud. There's a difference between seeing a cloud-ringed peak from afar, and actually being there — as the clouds are forced up the mountain, they're squeezed for snow, creating the thick layers of the stuff that lie all over the Windy Peaks and leaving a rainshadow on the other side. There's still some way to go before even the thinnest of the clouds are squeezed dry by the mountain, but the icy water dewing upon your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] and [pc.armor] conspires to make your ascent even more miserable, wicking away the warmth from your body.

        ...Yeah, being in the clouds is much more fun in one's imagination than it is in reality. When one gets down to it, it's just a cold, heavy fog.
rows.translation:
当你继续沿着山间小径前行时，干燥的空气突然变成了刺骨的雾气，你不禁打了个寒颤，这才意识到这种突然变化的原因：你正在穿过一片云层。从远处眺望被云雾环绕的山峰与真正置身其中是截然不同的——当云层被逼迫向上移动时，其中的雪分会被挤压出来，从而形成覆盖在风啸峰群上的厚厚积雪，而在云层的另一侧，则会留下雨影区。虽然距离那些最稀薄的云层被山峰完全吸收还有一段距离，但那些凝结在你身上的冰凉露水已经说明[pc.skinFurScalesNoun]以及[pc.armor]这些因素共同作用，让你的攀登过程变得更加艰难，还会使你体内的热量逐渐流失。

        ……是啊，在想象中，身处云层中肯定比实际情况要有趣得多。但事实上，那只不过是一层寒冷而浓重的雾而已。

rows.original: Here, the road from the elevator finally meets the mountain trail once again, the latter ending as it joins with the former. It's good to have an actual mountain road instead of cutting one's feet on the rough trail; although there's still the upwards ascent to battle, at least it isn't as hard on the feet as before. There's more than the cold, too: the air is getting thinner at this altitude, making it harder to breathe; inside the Undermountain, its earthen shell keeps the air under pressure and thick regardless of elevation, while there's no such privilege on its exterior, forcing you to gasp for breath every now and then. You're still a goodly distance from the peak, not that one would be heading up there at any point, right?
rows.translation: 在这里，电梯出口处的道路终于再次与山间小径汇合，后者在与之相连的地方结束了。有了一条真正的山路可走，总比在崎岖的小路上艰难行进要好得多；虽然仍然需要向上攀登，但至少足部不会像之前那样受到折磨了。不仅仅是寒冷的问题：在这样的高度，空气会变得越来越稀薄，从而导致呼吸变得困难；在地下山脉的内部，其土质外壳能够使空气保持一定的压力和密度，无论处于什么高度，而在外部则没有这样的保护机制，因此你不得不时不时地喘上几口气。你距离顶峰还有相当长的距离呢，不过其实也没人会真的去往那个地方吧？

rows.original:
An old bridge of minotaur make that looks to date from before the Godswar. Arches dominate its style with closely fitted masonry and ancient concrete as it spans across a deep ravine, sturdy and still standing despite having weathered conditions in the Windy Peaks all these decades. Low parapets offer less resistance to the wind, yet are sufficient to keep most people from plummeting to their doom; given how the stone is lightly iced-over, a smattering of gravel has been set into the concrete finish to provide traction.

        South of the bridge landing, the remnants of a minotaur village stand, now little more than the broken shells and skeletons of once-sturdy, perhaps even beautiful buildings. Why there would be people living here by the bridge is anyone's guess, but why they left is quite obvious: with the way some of the homes have been torn apart by giant teeth and claws, their markings still evident on the architecture, the people who lived here didn't even attempt to put up any resistance and instead fled for the safety of the mountain's interior. That the bridge still stands despite the destruction that surrounds it implies that the wraiths' armies were capable of recognizing value, savage as they may have been...
rows.translation:
那座由弥诺陶洛斯建造的古老桥梁，看起来似乎可以追溯到神战之前。它的设计以拱门结构为主，使用了紧密拼接的石材和古老的混凝土材料。这座桥横跨一条深深的峡谷，尽管在这些年代里经历了风啸峰地区恶劣的自然环境，但它依然坚固地矗立在那里。较低的护栏对风的阻力较小，但足以防止大多数人从高处坠落；由于石面上覆盖着一层薄冰，因此在混凝土表面撒了一些碎石，以增加摩擦力。

        在桥头南侧，残存着一座弥诺陶洛斯人的村庄。如今，那里只剩下那些曾经坚固甚至堪称美丽的建筑物的残骸和骨架。究竟为什么还会有人住在桥边这个地方，谁也说不清楚；但他们为什么离开，却一目了然——从那些被巨齿和巨爪撕得支离破碎的房屋来看，那些居住在这里的人们甚至没有尝试过抗性，而是直接逃往了山里的安全地带。尽管周围一片废墟，但这座桥依然屹立不倒，这一事实说明，那些幽灵军团虽然凶残残暴，却依然懂得什么是价值……

rows.original:
The northern side of the old minotaur bridge, this half may have been in more disrepair, but you note places where the Belharans attempted to combine their craftsmanship style with that of the minotaurs', with reasonable success. Short-lived as it may have been compared to the historical span of their imperium, the Belharans' tenure in the Marches at least attempted to improve and expand on infrastructure with the help of the locals.

        The northern side of the crossing offers an excellent view into the ravine below — narrow and deep, like the stream that flows through it. Even at this distance, the faint roar of rushing snowmelt reaches your hearing: this is where the chill of the peaks meets the heat of the Undermountain, producing this swift flow. As your eye follows the ravine, multiple such streams join together to create the source of the River Ridell that winds through the Undermountain, by your wayfort, and eventually out to sea.
rows.translation:
在老弥诺陶洛斯桥的北侧，这一半区域或许状况更为糟糕，但你可以看到一些地方——贝拉尔人试图将他们的建筑技艺与弥诺陶洛斯人的风格相结合，而且取得了一定的成功。尽管与他们帝国的历史跨度相比，贝拉尔人在边境地区的统治时间显得极为短暂，但他们至少在当地人的帮助下，努力改善并扩展了基础设施。

        穿过这片地带的北部区域，可以清楚地看到下方的峡谷——那里狭窄而深邃，就像流经其中的那条小溪一样。即使在这个距离上，你也能听到融雪奔流的微弱声响：正是这里，高山的寒意与地下山脉的热量交汇在一起，才形成了这种湍急的水流。当你顺着峡谷的方向望去，会发现许多这样的小溪汇聚在一起，最终形成了里德尔河的源头。这条河流蜿蜒穿过地下山脉，经过你的路标所在之处，最终流入大海。

rows.original:
The trail here slowly slopes down the river ravine, eventually running along the water's edge. Fast-flowing and foaming, the stream of snowmelt roars along with rocky bed, the water capped with white; the high walls of the ravine offer some shelter from the snow and wind, and although one must face the stiff breeze that follows the river's flow it's nevertheless much better than tha gales that sweep the exposed mountainside. All manner of small animals have taken refuge in here — although you don't see them directly, all the snow collected at the ravine's bottom is thick enough for their tracks to persist.

        Several vulperine fishing huts stand on the far side of the river, comfortably distant from the trail yet with enough space to see anyone approaching with plenty of warning. There isn't much wood on these mountain slopes — one wonders whether it was dragged up from the foothills, or sourced as mushrooms from within the mountain. The inhabitants don't seem to be around, and you get the impression that they're going to be staying that way so long as you're in the area.
rows.translation:
这条小径沿着河谷缓缓向下延伸，最终抵达了河岸边。融雪形成的溪流湍急而汹涌，带着泡沫沿着岩石铺就的河床奔流而下，水面被白色的泡沫覆盖着。河谷的高耸岩壁为人们提供了一定的遮蔽，使人们能够免受大雪和强风的侵袭。虽然仍然要面对顺着河流方向吹来的强劲寒风，但这样的环境还是比那些肆虐在裸露的山坡上的暴风要好得多。各种各样的小动物都躲到了这里——虽然你直接看不到它们，但山谷下装堆积的雪足够厚，因此它们的足迹能够清晰地留在雪地上。

        在河的对岸，有几间狐狸造的渔舍，它们距离小路有一段距离，因此可以及时发现任何靠近的人。这些山坡上的木材并不多——人们不禁会想，这些木材究竟是从山脚处运上来的，还是从山体内采集而来的。周围似乎也没有居民，给人的感觉是，只要你还在这个区域，这些山坡上就永远不会有居民出现。

rows.original:
A macabre sight greets you as you step atop this ledge: laid out atop a stone platform stand a trio of spires fashioned from golden metal, if not outright gold. Despite the winds here being just about strong enough to blow anyone unsecured off the mountainside, the platform and spires are in pristine condition; that can't be said for the skeletal remains that've gathered about the bases of said spires. Some of them look like they might have come from harpies, others from more heavyset races; all of them are distinctly humanoid. If that weren't enough, there's still a single forlorn skeleton rattling in the wind along with the chains that bind it to the golden spire, waiting to fall apart and join the massed bones at the base. The gleaming of gold, polished by the winds to the point where you can see your reflection in the metal pillars, juxtaposed against the dried, moldering bones that lie strewn about the platform forlornly — it's enough to set a sensation of unease in the pit of one's stomach.

        This is definitely not of Belharan or Minoan make, yet is too fine to actually have been fashioned by harpy hands. If not for its pristine appearance, one might reasonably assume it predates the arrival of either people to the Marches... or does it simply not age?
        
        A tribulation ground, an execution ground, a sacrificial ground... or perhaps all three at once. Thankfully, it doesn't look like the people who carry out these rituals keep an eye on this place, but one would expect that whatever divine or mystical force that animates this entire business has some means of keeping these golden spires from being disturbed in an unwanted fashion. Thieves would've long since pilfered them otherwise, right?
        
        Right?
rows.translation:
当你踏上这个岩架时，一幅令人不寒而栗的景象迎面扑来：在石制平台上，矗立着三座由黄金金属制成的尖塔，甚至可以说是纯金打造的。尽管这里的风大到足以将任何没有固定措施的人从山坡上吹下去，但这个平台以及那些尖塔却完好无损；然而，那些堆积在尖塔基部周围的骷髅遗骸，却无法保持这样的状态了。其中一些看起来似乎源自鹰身女妖，而另一些则更像是某些体格魁梧的种族；但它们全都具备明显的人形特征。如果这些还不够的话，还有一具孤独的骷髅在风中摇晃着，那些将它束缚在金色尖塔上的链条也在随风摆动，等待着最终解体，然后加入那些堆积在塔基处的骨头之中。那些被风吹得闪闪发光的黄金，其表面光滑到甚至可以在金属柱子上看到自己的倒影；而那些散落在平台上的干枯、发霉的骨头，则形成了一种鲜明的对比……这一切足以让人感到一阵不安，让胃里产生一种莫名的紧张感。

        这绝对不是贝尔哈兰人或米诺斯人制作的，但它太过精致，不可能是由那些粗陋的手工打造的。如果不是因为它那完好无损的外观，人们很可能会认为它早在这两个民族来到这片边境地区之前就已经存在了……还是说，它根本就不会衰老呢？
        
        一处苦难之地，一处刑场，一处献祭之地……或许同时兼具这三重意义。幸运的是，看起来那些举行这些仪式的人并没有特别关注这个地方，但人们也会想，究竟是哪种神圣或神秘的力量在维系着这一切，才会让这些金色的尖塔免于受到不必要的干扰。否则，盗贼早就把它们偷走了，对吧？
        
        对吧？

rows.original:
A long tunnel that winds under the peaks, completely dark inside — if not for the steady draft blowing from one end to the other, you wouldn't know that there was an exit on the other end. The tunnel itself is remarkably straight, too much to have been the work of a giant burrowing creature like that on the lower slopes — it's simply a line from one end to the other without any twists or turns.

        Yet this doesn't seem like the work of excavators or engineers, either. The walls may be exempt, but one would expect the ground to be smoothed if this were meant to be a road... and then one looks closer to note that the walls look as if they'd once been molten. Perhaps some powerful spell was once cast here to simply burn through so much rock... but then the question remains: why?
        
        All that, alas, is in the past.
rows.translation:
一条蜿蜒穿过山峰下方的长隧道，内部一片漆黑——要不是有着一股持续不断地从一端吹向另一端的气流，你根本不会知道隧道的另一端有一处出口。这条隧道本身也非常笔直，这样的走向显然不可能是那些生活在低坡地区的巨型挖掘生物建造的；它简直就是一条从起点直达终点的直线，没有任何弯道或转折。

        然而，这看起来也不像是挖掘机或工程师的作品。虽然墙壁可能没有受到破坏，但如果是打算修建一条道路的话，地面应该会被平整才对……仔细观察后，人们会发现这些墙壁似乎曾经被熔化过。也许曾经有人在这里施展了某种强大的法术，从而将如此大量的岩石彻底烧毁……但问题依然存在：为什么呢？
        
        可惜，这一切都已经成为了过去。

rows.original: The trampled and smashed remains of a low stone fence are all that denote the boundaries of what could conceivably be called a backyard — a border where civilization ends and the wilderness begins. Even if snow and time have buried much of the past, it's still clear that some violent clash once took place here. Even the harpies living close by instinctively give this particular snowfield a wide berth despite being as thick as thieves all around, and you feel the urge to hurry through.
rows.translation: 那些被踩踏得支离破碎的低矮石栏，才是那片勉强可以称之为“后院”的区域的边界——一个文明终结、荒野开始的地方。尽管积雪和时间的侵蚀已经掩盖了许多过去的痕迹，但这里曾经发生过激烈的冲突，这一点依然清晰可见。就连那些生活在附近的鹰身女妖，也出于本能地避开这片雪地；尽管它们到处都是，但你还是会忍不住想要尽快穿过这里。
rows.raw: "\n        The trampled and smashed remains of a low stone fence are all that denote the boundaries of what could conceivably be called a backyard — a border where civilization ends and the wilderness begins. Even if snow and time have buried much of the past, it's still clear that some violent clash once took place here. Even the harpies living close by instinctively give this particular snowfield a wide berth despite being as thick as thieves all around, and you feel the urge to hurry through."

rows.original:
The single-storey buildings on this side of the imperial resort are more tightly spaced and a lot less glamorous than those on the western side — servants' quarters, then, for those in the dignitaries' retinues. Unheated, too, but that hasn't stopped harpies from piling into the multitude of dormitories; crumbling as they are from decades of feathered occupation, the walls and roofs are still sturdy, making them much better living arrangements than the average harpy nest.

        Of course, while nice, the living conditions aren't the real prize here. Being able to be close to their matron and rub shoulders with the well-connected — well, peoples of all times and races have endured worse conditions than these to have even the flimsiest claim to be living where it's happening. If anything, they're even more tightly packed than the heated villas thanks to their close proximity to the main building to the north...
rows.translation:
皇宫度假区这一侧的单层建筑间距更为紧密，也远没有西侧那些建筑那么华丽——这些地方应该是为贵族随从们准备的仆人住所。这些房屋并没有配备暖气设施，但这并没有阻止那些女妖们挤进这些众多的宿舍里。虽然经过数十年的居住，墙壁和屋顶已经破旧不堪，但它们仍然相当坚固，因此这些住所比普通的女妖巢穴要舒适得多。

        当然，虽然生活条件不错，但这也并非真正的关键所在。能够接近那些有影响力的人，与那些关系广泛的人交往——事实上，历代各族的人们为了能够置身于这些重要事件的中心，都曾忍受过比这更糟糕的条件。事实上，由于它们紧邻北侧的主楼，因此它们的布局甚至比那些带暖气的别墅还要紧凑……

rows.original:
As one finally draws close to the imperial outpost, the realization that it's not an outpost at all dawns: the buildings aren't of a military or industrial nature, but the remnants of luxury villas such as the minotaurs would build, but with a layer of Belharan aesthetics laid over them. Accommodations for the wealthy and well-connected, there's still some grandeur in these long-abandoned abodes — and judging from the raucous caucus coming from within, absolutely packed with harpies. Not exactly a conventional nest for their kind, perhaps, but even these bird-brains know luxury when one sees it. They've tried to keep the old villas in shape and decorate them to their own harpy tastes, and even if their handiwork isn't perfect the warmth that radiates from these old stone shells proves that the piping that the Belharans wrought to heat their summer homes with steam from the hot wells is still functional.

        Even if they were the wealthy elite, that the Belharan imperials had the means to drag people and material all the way to the edges of their lands and commission the construction of a mountain resort for the sake of getting away from it all... such a waste for harpies to be squatting in the ruins of their civilisation, but that's how it is.
rows.translation:
当人们终于接近那座所谓的帝国前哨站时，才会突然意识到：它根本就不是什么前哨站。那些建筑物既不具有军事用途，也不属于工业设施，而是类似弥诺陶洛斯会建造的豪华别墅的遗迹，只不过在这些遗迹之上叠加了一层贝拉兰式的审美风格。这些早已被废弃的居所，依然保留着一些奢华的气息——从里面传出来的喧闹声来看，里面肯定挤满了那些吵闹的人。对于他们这种生物来说，这或许并不是一个传统的栖息之地，但即便是这些头脑简单的人，也能分辨出什么是奢华。他们努力维护这些古老别墅的原貌，并按照自己独特的品味对它们进行装饰。虽然他们的手艺并不完美，但这些古老石屋散发出的温暖气息，证明了贝尔哈兰人当年为给夏季居所提供热水而建造的蒸汽系统至今依然可以使用。

        即便他们是那些富有的精英，贝拉兰帝国也有能力将人们和物资运送到他们疆域的边远地区，甚至专门建造山地度假胜地， just为了远离尘世的喧嚣与纷扰。让鹰身女妖们栖息在她们文明的废墟中，真是太浪费了……但事实就是如此。

rows.original: As one approaches the buildings in the distance, the road becomes ever more grandiose: though they may be chipped and scuffed by the weather and heavy snow, the carved flagstones still carry some of the beauty and grandeur that they once had. The same can't be said of the roadside statues, now only plinths and stumps as a result of... well, whatever the harpies carried them off for. A scene originally meant to be impressive and welcoming is now quite the foreboding picture, and the occasional harpy song from above doesn't help, either. Various stone markers stand by the roadside, but whatever they're signing to, the words have long since been worn away.
rows.translation: 当人们逐渐接近远处的那些建筑时，道路也变得越来越宏伟壮观：尽管这些石板路在风雨和厚重的积雪中已经出现了裂痕和磨损，但那些雕刻精美的石板依然保留着它们曾经拥有的那份美丽与庄严。路边的雕像们却无法幸免——如今只剩下基座和残骸，因为……嗯，那些鹰身女妖把它们带去了哪里吧。原本应该令人印象深刻、营造出欢迎氛围的场景，现在却显得阴森恐怖，而偶尔从上方传来的鹰身女妖的歌声，更是让这种氛围更加压抑。路旁竖立着各种石制标记，但无论它们原本刻着什么，那些文字早已被风化得面目全非了。

rows.original:
The road here curves around a stretch of mountain shelf, comfortably set in the wind-shadow of a particularly craggy peak to the east. Happily, one exchanges the risk of being blown off the mountainside with the risk of running into whatever lairs in the multiple caves set within said peak — the sheer number of frozen bones littered about their entrances implies an entire community of predatory animals that live within, which in turn has its own implications...

        There isn't enough prey of sufficient size on the peaks to sustain so many predators, and the remains suggest that said prey was gathered in the foothills and coastlands to either side of the mountains. Thankfully, there don't seem to be any sapient peoples amongst the remains... but you nevertheless note that the harpies give this particular crag a wide berth anyway.
        
        [flags.KAILANI_MET
            |Out of caution, you look up to the dead tree jutting out from the crag's face. As far as you can tell, all is as it should be...
        ]
rows.translation:
这条道路沿着一片山脊蜿蜒而行，东侧有一座岩石嶙峋的山峰，它的阴影为道路提供了良好的遮蔽。幸运的是，人们所要面对的风险，从被山风吹下山坡，转变为可能会遇到那座山峰中众多洞穴里潜藏的未知生物——那些散落在洞穴入口处的累累白骨，显然表明那里生活着整个一群捕食性动物，而这一事实自然也会带来其他种种影响。

        这些山峰上并没有足够多、体型足够的猎物来养活这么多捕食者，而从遗留物来看，这些猎物应该是从山脉两侧的丘陵地带和沿海地区捕获的。幸运的是，这些遗留物中似乎并没有任何智慧生物的痕迹。不过你还是注意到，那些鹰身女妖们无论如何都会避开这块特殊的岩石。
        
        [flags.KAILANI_MET
            |出于谨慎，你抬头看了看从峭壁表面伸出来的那棵枯树。就你所能看到的范围而言，一切看起来都正常无异……
        ]

rows.original:
The road here passes under several precipitous overhangs — the Minoans of the past had the foresight to support said treacherous landforms with several of their signature arches, preventing them from collapsing onto the road below. Columns in the form of regal bulls and cowgirls hold up the roofs of said arches as if balancing water jugs on their heads, their arms extended in welcome.

        Perhaps once upon a time these peaks were more hospitable and less wind-blasted than they are now; much of the old infrastructure has clearly been built with a milder climate in mind. Not that it hasn't held up since then and the harpies themselves have little interest in maintaining roads when they can fly... but it does lead one to wonder.
rows.translation:
这条道路从几处陡峭的岩壁下方穿过——过去的米诺斯人具有远见卓识，他们用自己特有的拱桥结构支撑住了这些危险的地质构造，从而防止它们坍塌下来压到下面的道路上。那些形如威严公牛和牛仔女的角色，仿佛将水壶稳稳地顶在头上一般，支撑着那些拱门的顶部，她们的手臂伸展开来，仿佛在热情地欢迎着人们。

        或许在某个遥远的时代，这些山峰曾经更加宜人，也不像现在这样经常受到强风的侵袭；很明显，许多古老的基础设施都是建立在气候较为温和的条件下建造的。虽然从那以后，这些道路依然能够使用，而且那些鹰身女妖们既然会飞行，自然也不会太在意维护这些道路……但这也让人不禁产生一些疑问。

"

rows.original:
The road here broadens even further, terraces cut into the mountainside — stretches of flat ground divided by ramps imply that it was meant more for vehicles than people on foot. As to how a cart or carriage would get up all the way to the peaks... well there's that elevator you saw earlier. That being said, your thighs are thankful for the opportunity to not be constantly battling an ascent...

        How long did it take to level this road, one wonders, let alone surface it? How much work did it take to bring the materials up this high? That the civilizations of the past would simply perform such feats for seemingly trivial reasons boggles the mind.
rows.translation:
这条路在这里变得更加宽阔，山体上开凿出了层层梯田；那些被斜坡分隔开的平坦地带显然更适用于车辆通行，而非行人行走。至于如何让马车或货车一路行驶到山顶，那就另当别论了。嗯，就是你之前看到的那部电梯。话说回来，你的大腿肯定也很庆幸有机会不用一直费力地上升了……

        人们不禁会想，修筑这条道路究竟花了多长时间，更不用说把它铺平了…… 将这些材料运送到这么高的地方，究竟需要耗费多少人力和物力呢？想到过去的文明们仅仅因为一些看似微不足道的理由，就能完成这样的壮举，实在令人惊叹不已。

rows.original:
A frozen-over lake that branches off from the mountain stream — the ice seems thick and solid underfoot, enough to support your weight, and there's evidence of temporary vulperine shelters that've been set up by the lakeside at various points in the past. Ice fishing, and quite regularly too, judging by the amount of discarded offal frozen in the snow that scavengers haven't gotten to yet.

        Once, this might have been part of the stream's main course, but as the waters cut a new path down the mountainside the flows slowed and froze over, resulting in a crescent-shaped lake. The high walls of the lake ravine help keep the air within relatively calm despite the howling winds overhead, and that's allowed all kinds of odd life to flourish within, from ice roses more common to the northern glacial rift to lotuses that push through the thick ice and spread blossoms and leaves alike to catch the sun.
rows.translation:
一片从山间溪流延伸而来的结冰湖泊——脚下的冰层看起来厚实而坚固，足以承受你的体重。而且，在过去的某个时候，人们曾在湖边不同位置搭建过临时性的庇护所。根据雪中被遗弃的、尚未被食腐动物啃食的动物内脏数量来看，人们进行冰钓的活动应该相当频繁。  

        曾经，这条小溪的水流可能是这条河流的主要通道之一，但随着水流在山体上开辟出新的路径，水流速度变缓，最终冻结形成了一个新月形的湖泊。尽管头顶上风声呼啸，但这片湖泊峡谷的高耸墙壁使得内部的空气相对平静，这种环境为各种奇特的生物提供了生存条件——从在北方冰川裂谷中常见的冰玫瑰，到那些突破厚厚的冰层、绽放出花朵和叶子来吸收阳光的莲花，它们都在这里繁衍生息。

rows.original:
A slope breaks the northern side of the ravine walls here, leading down to the water's edge. Looking as if it'd been torn out of the stone by some gargantuan beast, it provides relatively safe passage to and from the bottom, if one doesn't mind the journey. Steep walls rise to either side of the slope, honeycombed with a multitude of cave entrances; one could imagine that the selfsame beast that created this slope was some kind of giant borer worm, given how absolutely riddled with holes the ravine walls are.

        The caves themselves, alas, offer little by way of interesting exploration. Even before the [dayNight|sun|moon]light gives out, one can see that the caves and tunnels dip below the water table of the adjoining stream, flooded ages ago. Even with the ability to breathe water, any would-be spelunker would need to resist the bitterly cold temperatures as well.
rows.translation:
这里的峡谷北壁被一道斜坡打断，斜坡一直通向水边。它看起来像是被某头庞然巨兽从岩石中硬生生撕出来的；只要不介意这段路程，它便能提供一条较为安全的通道，往返谷底。斜坡两侧耸立着陡峭的岩壁，上面布满蜂窝般的洞窟入口。峡谷岩壁被挖得千疮百孔，让人不禁想象，挖出这道斜坡的也许是某种巨型钻地蠕虫。

        可惜，这些洞窟本身并没有多少值得探索的地方。甚至在[dayNight|日光|月光]完全消失之前，人们就能看出这些洞窟和隧道向下延伸到了附近溪流的地下水位以下，早在很久以前就被淹没了。即使能在水下呼吸，想进去探洞的人也必须抵御那刺骨的低温。

rows.translation: [QUEST_CRYSTAL_CLEAR2.stateRange 0 |你才刚刚开始进入这个洞穴；外面的光线已经[dayNight |太阳 |月亮 ]光线依然从洞穴的入口处照射进来，为你的前行之路照亮了道路。这个洞穴比你想象中要宽敞得多：有足够的空间供你通行。[party.som | 独自面对两次同样的困境 | 以及[comp1.name]并肩站在一起 | 以及[comp1.name]并排站在一起，尽管这样的安排对你们两人来说可能还不够[comp2.name]那个不得不殿后的人 ]墙壁在大部分区域都显得崎岖而布满灰尘，但有些地方却被磨得光滑，或是留下了划痕。 洞穴向东延伸，地势越来越低，崎岖不平的地面仿佛在引导你深入风啸峰的地底，仿佛想要将你整个吞没进去。在你的西侧是洞穴的入口；你仍然能感受到寒风的刺骨，也能闻到清新的山间空气，与洞穴内部那潮湿、闷热的恶臭形成了鲜明的对比。外界的光线在一段距离内为你的前行提供了照明，因此短时间内你不会遇到光线不足的问题。 |你才刚刚开始进入这个洞穴；外面的光线已经[dayNight|太阳|月亮]光线依然从洞穴的入口处照射进来，为你的前行之路照亮了道路。这个洞穴比你想象中要宽敞得多：有足够的空间让你和凯拉尼并排站立，甚至还能容纳另外四个人。洞壁的大部分地方都布满了崎岖的突起和灰尘，但也有部分地方被磨损或刮得变得光滑平整。 洞穴向东延伸，地势逐渐变得崎岖不平，仿佛要将你彻底吞没般将你引向风啸峰的山腹之中。而在你的西侧，则是洞穴的入口——你依然能感受到外面清风的寒意，也能闻到新鲜的山间空气，与洞穴内部那股潮湿、闷热的空气形成鲜明对比。外界的光线能够在一段距离内为你照亮前行的道路，因此短时间内你不会遇到自然光线不足的问题。 在你和凯拉尼完成既定目标之前，你们是无法回头的。 ]

rows.translation:
[QUEST_CRYSTAL_CLEAR2.stateRange 0
            |外部的光线已经开始变得有些昏暗，但还不至于让你无法清楚地看到前方一定距离内的景象——洞穴中的每一个弯道都变得越来越黑暗，不过你仍然能够分辨出周围洞穴中的那些细微结构。

            你现在所在的这个空间，就是你曾经发现那个奇怪的、长满毛发的、体型矮小的生物的地方。那种生物在房间里四处游荡时，会发出许多哨声。这个空间很宽敞，呈圆顶状；地面被整理得格外整洁，没有一块碎石，而墙壁在某些地方似乎还被打磨得非常光滑。

rows.original: [QUEST_CRYSTAL_CLEAR2.stateRange 0 |Traveling deeper into the cave leads you downward into the mountain. As you go, you notice that the topography starts to change: at the mouth of the cave, spires of stone jutted from both the roof and the floor, veiny with shiny minerals and misshapen from eras of wear from moisture and pressure. The deeper you go, though, the smoother everything gets: there are no stalagmites and the walls had been picked clean of the shinier stones before being sanded down smooth. Because nothing lives in this cave anymore, the place is starting to get a little messier: on top of dirt and dust beginning to pile up, pebbles and stones are beginning to litter the cave's floor as the elements slowly chip at the walls. The light from the mouth of the cave has difficulty reaching this far down, and visibly is starting to get poor. The last time you were here with Kailani, you could start seeing light and hearing noises coming from deeper inside the cave at this point. But now, there's nothing: the place is dead, dark, and quiet. |Traveling deeper into the cave leads you downward into the mountain. As you go, you notice that the topography starts to change: at the mouth of the cave, spires of stone jutted from both the roof and the floor, veiny with shiny minerals and misshapen from eras of wear from moisture and pressure. The deeper you go, though, the smoother everything gets: there are no stalagmites and the walls had been picked clean of the shinier stones before being sanded down smooth. Like in the cavity behind you, the floor had been meticulously swept clean of debris: the floor is dusty and dirty, but there are no pebbles or stones to stub your toes on. The light from the mouth of the cave has difficulty reaching this far down, and visibly is starting to get poor... but as you travel further west and deeper into the cave, the visibility slowly gets steadier and brighter. With every corner you and Kailani round, the lights get brighter... and you can hear something moving deeper in the cave. rows.translation: [QUEST_CRYSTAL_CLEAR2.stateRange 0 |越往洞穴深处走，你就越往下进入山体。随着你继续前进，你会注意到地形开始发生变化：在洞穴的入口处，石柱从洞顶和洞底突出出来，这些石柱上布满了闪闪发光的矿物质，由于长期受到水分和压力的侵蚀，它们已经变得形状扭曲。然而，当你越往深处走，一切就会变得越平整：那里没有钟乳石，墙壁上也已经被清理干净，那些较为闪亮的石头都被取走后，墙壁才被打磨得光滑平整。因为这个洞穴里已经没有任何生物居住了，所以这里开始变得有些杂乱——除了灰尘和污垢逐渐堆积之外，随着自然因素的侵蚀，小石子和碎石也开始散落在洞穴的地板上。 洞穴入口处的光线很难照射到这么深的地方，因此光线已经变得很微弱了。上次你和凯拉尼一起来这里的时候，在这个位置还能看到洞穴深处传来的光线，也能听到那里传来的声音。但现在，这里什么都没有：一片死寂，黑暗笼罩着一切，四周一片安静。 |越往洞穴深处走，你就越往下进入山体。随着你继续前进，你会注意到地形开始发生变化：在洞穴的入口处，石柱从洞顶和洞底突出出来，这些石柱上布满了闪闪发光的矿物质，由于长期受到水分和压力的侵蚀，它们已经变得形状扭曲。然而，当你越往深处走，一切就会变得越顺畅：那里没有钟乳石，墙壁上也已经被清理干净，那些较为闪亮的石头都被取走后，墙壁才被打磨得光滑平整。就像你身后的这个洞穴一样，地面也被仔细地清扫得干干净净，没有一片碎屑；虽然地面上会有灰尘和污垢，但也不会有鹅卵石或石头让你踢到脚趾。 洞穴入口处的光线很难照射到这么深的地方，因此可见度正在逐渐下降……但当你继续向西前进，深入洞穴的内部时，可见度会慢慢变得稳定起来，光线也会变得明亮一些。每当你们和凯拉尼绕过一个拐角，灯光就会变得更加明亮……同时，你们也能听到洞穴深处有东西在移动。你们正在追逐的那只野兽就在附近。[flags.KAILANI_MON 1 |从它那沉重的脚步声来看，它正以一种悠闲的速度巡视着自己的“领地”，对周围的环境显得十分放松、毫无戒备。它根本不知道你们两个就在那里。因此，你们仍然拥有出其不意的机会。 | 从那些沉重而急促的脚步声，以及那些低吼声和哨声所构成的杂乱声响来看，那只生物显然处于紧张状态，且随时保持警惕。你们一开始进入这个洞穴时所拥有的任何优势，现在都已经荡然无存了。 ] 你最好做好心理准备：继续深入这个洞穴的话，就再也没办法出来了！ ]

rows.original: This storeroom is what will eventually turn into your vault... or at least, so you think. It's recognizable as such thanks to the shape of the room, as well as the wall and door — those haven't changed with the years. Of course, the portcullis is a dead giveaway, considering how the mechanism's built into the keep's structure itself. Instead of valuables, though, this place was used to store sundries — dusty jars, boxes and barrels line the walls, succumbing to dry rot along with their contents. It's clear that there's nothing of use here, even if the containers themselves may be historical curiosities. Or maybe these were valuables during that time in the Wayfort's history...
rows.translation: 这个储藏室最终将会变成你的保险库……至少你是这么认为的。从房间的结构、墙壁以及门的设计来看，它确实具有保险库的特征——这些年来这些元素都没有发生任何变化。当然，那扇可升降的栅门更是暴露了它的真实用途，因为这种装置是直接建在城堡的结构中的。 然而，这个地方并不是用来存放贵重物品的，而是用来存放各种杂物——墙壁上排列着布满灰尘的罐子、箱子和桶，它们连同里面的物品一起都发生了干腐。很明显，这里没有任何有用的东西，即使这些容器本身可能具有历史价值。或者也可能是这些。是在荒废驿堡的历史中，那段时期里的一些珍贵物品……

rows.original: With the feathered fiend out of the way, the hallways have reshaped themselves into a stairwell leading up and out of this madness. The promise of sanity and stability beckons...
rows.translation: 随着那个长着羽毛的恶魔被消灭，这些走廊重新变形成了一条通往外界的楼梯。理智与稳定的希望正在召唤着人们……
rows.raw: "\n        With the feathered fiend out of the way, the hallways have reshaped themselves into a stairwell leading up and out of this madness. The promise of sanity and stability beckons..."

rows.original:
You're standing outside what will eventually become your vault and armory, just outside the heavy doors. It's disorienting in a way, as if the maze of hallways and broken masonry you traversed to get out of the storeroom was never there — you can even see right back into it from here. And yet if you were to take a step back into that doorway, you'd find yourself right back in that space...

        Does it actually exist to begin with? Or is it all in your mind, and you're merely walking in place while navigating that mind-bending maze?
        
        Well. With the rest of the Wayfort's past laid out before you, hopefully it won't be an issue.
rows.translation:
你此刻站在那扇厚重的大门之外，这里最终将会成为你的金库和武器库。这种场景在某种程度上会让人感到迷失方向，因为那些你曾经穿越过的迷宫般的走廊和破损的砖石结构，仿佛从来就不存在过——从这里你甚至可以直接看到那个储藏室的内部。然而，如果你再走一步回到那个门口，你会发现自己又回到了那个空间里……

        这个空间究竟是否存在呢？还是说这一切都只存在于你的脑海中，而你只是在那个令人费解的迷宫中兜圈子而已？
        
        嗯，既然荒废驿堡过去的那些事情都已经向你交代清楚了，希望这不会成为什么问题。
rows.raw:
"
        You're standing outside what will eventually become your vault and armory, just outside the heavy doors. It's disorienting in a way, as if the maze of hallways and broken masonry you traversed to get out of the storeroom was never there — you can even see right back into it from here. And yet if you were to take a step back into that doorway, you'd find yourself right back in that space...

        Does it actually exist to begin with? Or is it all in your mind, and you're merely walking in place while navigating that mind-bending maze?
        
        Well. With the rest of the Wayfort's past laid out before you, hopefully it won't be an issue."

rows.original: The remains of bunks — so that's where those came from when you first found them. Solid enough to survive a couple centuries' worth of exposure, and the bunks in this mirrored image of the Wayfort's past are no exception. If not for the dust, some of them even look serviceable... Out of curiosity, you step past them into what will be your private bedchambers in the far future. Yes... the enormous affair of mahogany and wolfhide certainly isn't your bed, but even though it looks recently slept in its previous owner is likely just another one of the shattered psyches wandering these halls. A heavy aura of peaceful restfulness hangs over this place like a heavy velvet curtain; you think that this might be the only actually safe place in this entire shattered image.
rows.translation: 那些床铺的残骸——原来你最初发现它们的时候，它们就是从这里来的。这些床铺足够坚固，能够经受几个世纪的风雨侵蚀，而这个反映荒废驿堡过去生活的场景中的床铺也不例外。要不是积满了灰尘，其中一些甚至看起来还能继续使用…… 出于好奇，你走过去，那些地方在未来将会成为你的私人卧室。没错……那些由桃花心木和狼皮制成的巨大床铺，确实非常豪华你的一张床，但尽管它看起来像是有人最近使用过，它的前主人很可能只是那些在这片废墟中游荡的、精神崩溃的人中的一个罢了。 一股宁静而安详的气息笼罩着这个地方，就像一道厚重的天鹅绒帷幕；你会觉得，这可能是整个这片废墟中唯一真正安全的地方了。
rows.raw: " The remains of bunks — so that's where those came from when you first found them. Solid enough to survive a couple centuries' worth of exposure, and the bunks in this mirrored image of the Wayfort's past are no exception. If not for the dust, some of them even look serviceable... Out of curiosity, you step past them into what will be your private bedchambers in the far future. Yes... the enormous affair of mahogany and wolfhide certainly isn't your bed, but even though it looks recently slept in its previous owner is likely just another one of the shattered psyches wandering these halls. A heavy aura of peaceful restfulness hangs over this place like a heavy velvet curtain; you think that this might be the only actually safe place in this entire shattered image."

rows.original:
A mostly bare kitchen garden — looks like with the cessation of outside provisioning, the garrison attempted to stave off the inevitable by taking a crash course in gardening. A few leaves and stems sway in a breeze that doesn't exist, preserved by the cessation of time and the memories of those trapped here. This... this is supposed to be where your kitchen is in the future, right? Why is it open to the air? Vegetables and herbs for cooking, none of which look healthy... but it's completely at odds with what you know.

        The discrepancies usually aren't that great, but this takes the cake. At least it's vaguely food related... there may be something of use here amidst the dry soil and desiccated plants.
rows.translation:
这个厨房花园几乎什么都没有——看来，当外部补给中断后，驻军们为了延缓不可避免的结局，仓促地开始学习园艺。几片树叶和茎秆在微风中轻轻摇曳，而这阵微风其实并不存在，只是被时间的长河以及那些被困在这里的人们的记忆所保留下来的罢了。这个……这里应该是你未来厨房的位置吧？为什么它是露天的呢？用来烹饪的蔬菜和香草，看起来一点都不健康……但这完全与你所了解的情况相悖啊。

        通常这种差异不会太大，但这次真的太过分了。至少它与食物有点关系……在这些干涸的土壤和枯萎的植物中，或许能找到一些有用的东西。

"

rows.original:
This... you can only assume that it's your grand hall, given the size of it. All the furniture one might expect of a hall has been replaced with rows of broken bunks, the vast space turned into a makeshift hospital in the last days of the Wayfort's occupancy. Only the long table remains in place, probably because it was too heavy to be moved; corroded surgeons' instruments and jars lie upon it, along with a heavy brass cauldron off to the side. Stale straw lines the masonry floor while wooden partitions and curtains have been set up to afford the convalescent some kind of privacy, all to little effect.

        The doors, you note, are in the process of being blown inwards — cracking, shattered, splinters suspended in animation as the flow of time has stopped. Well, at least now you know what dealt that damage.
rows.translation:
这个地方……考虑到它的规模，你只能认为它曾经是你的大厅。那些通常会出现在大厅里的家具都被替换成了成排的破旧床铺，在荒废驿堡家族居住的最后几天，这个巨大的空间被临时改成了医院。只有那张长桌还原封不动地摆在那里，大概是因为它太重了，根本搬不动；一些生锈的外科手术器械和罐子被放在桌上，旁边还放着一个重型的黄铜大锅。发霉的稻草铺满了石砌的地面，而木制的隔板和窗帘也被架了起来，试图为康复中的病人提供一些隐私，但这些措施几乎没有什么效果。

        你会发现，那些门正在被向外炸开——它们正在开裂、碎裂，碎片仿佛被时间静止的力量所定格，悬在半空中。好吧，至少现在你知道是什么造成了这样的破坏了。

Stale straw lines the masonry floor while wooden partitions and curtains have been set up to afford the convalescent some kind of privacy, all to little effect.

rows.original:
At least the mess hall where Rumie's bar will be hasn't changed that much in either form or function — it's ingrained into the walls at this point, a place where people gather to eat, drink and make merry. That being said, no doubt there was a dire lack of the latter in the Wayfort's last days... the atmosphere of merriment that should pervade to-be-Rumie's bar is completely and utterly lacking.

        The suddenness with which everything apart is startling, even if not surprising. Maybe there's still something to be had in the still-intact casks.
rows.translation:
至少，露米酒吧所在的那个食堂，无论是外观还是功能，都没有发生太大的变化——它早已成为了这个地方不可或缺的一部分，人们在这里聚在一起吃饭、喝酒、欢庆。不过，可以肯定的是，在荒废驿堡的最后那些日子里，这里显然已经没有了欢庆的气氛。……本该充斥在即将成为“露米酒吧”地方的欢乐氛围，却完全不存在。

        一切都突然变得如此不同，这种反差虽然并不令人意外，但却令人震惊。或许，那些尚未被打开的酒桶里，还藏着些什么值得期待的东西。

rows.original:
A throne of bone and furs stands atop a dais on the south side of the hall, decrepit and dusty; despite its disrepair, a commanding aura still lingers about such a rickety piece of furniture that you're half-expecting the sundered shade of the Wayfort's previous commander to manifest and leap at you.

        Fortunately, no such thing happens. Despite the psychic pressure that the throne exudes, strong enough for even you to sense it, you remain unaccosted. [flags.NINA_JUICE
            |Under the influence of Nina's Juice, though, you're able to clearly see the intense purple aura surrounding it. Despite its appearance, it doesn't feel malevolent, more... expectant, if anything.
        ]
rows.translation:
在大厅的南侧，一个由骨头和毛皮制成的王座矗立在高台上，它显得破旧而布满灰尘；尽管如此，这种残破的家具依然散发着一种令人敬畏的气息，让你几乎以为会看到荒废驿堡前任指挥官的幽灵现身并向你扑来。

        幸运的是，这样的事情并没有发生。尽管这个王座散发出的灵力压力足以让你感受到，但你却丝毫没有受到任何干扰。 [flags.NINA_JUICE
            |然而，在尼娜之汁的作用下，你能够清楚地看到它周围那股强烈的紫色光环。尽管它看起来如此，但它并不会给人一种邪恶的感觉，反而更像是……充满期待。
        ]

rows.original:
The foyer looks to have been the site of a battle — bones and tarnished weapons lie scattered amidst the rubble from smashed arches, yellowed remains that haven't been moved for only the gods know how long. It's likely that magic was used, considering the scorch marks on the archway pillars and craters in the ground; not a single one of the archways remains standing, marble chunks scattered all over.

        The remains look to have come from a variety of peoples — you recognize what likely are minotaur, boreal elf and lupines amidst the dead. At least that gives an idea of who the garrisoned defenders were, even if their deaths weren't pretty. The Wayfort was a boreal elf holding back in the day, wasn't it? Things must've gotten pretty bad for people to band together this unquestioningly.
rows.translation:
大厅看来曾经发生过一场激烈的战斗——骨头和生锈的武器散落在破碎的拱门残骸之中，那些已经泛黄的遗迹不知被遗弃了多久。从拱门柱子上留下的烧焦痕迹以及地面上的坑洞来看，很可能使用了魔法；所有的拱门都已经倒塌，大理石碎片四处散落。

        这些遗骸似乎属于不同种族的人——在死者中，你能辨认出可能是弥诺陶洛斯、极北精灵以及狼族。至少这能让我们大致了解那些驻守在这里的防御者究竟是谁，尽管他们的死亡过程一定很惨烈。荒废驿堡当年应该是个保守、守旧的极北精灵吧？情况肯定已经变得非常糟糕，否则人们也不会如此毫不犹豫地团结起来。

It's likely that magic was used, considering the scorch marks on the archway pillars and craters in the ground; not a single one of the archways remains standing, marble chunks scattered all over.

rows.original: Heavy fighting took place in this hallway; furniture and rubble have been piled up into makeshift barricades that were eventually overrun. Deep gashes and gouges mark the old masonry walls, angular chunks torn out by great claws of some kind. Several arrowheads remain scattered on the floor amidst the bodies of the defenders, shafts rotted away long ago; one notices to one's unsettling dismay that the attackers were either so effective as to not suffer a single loss, or they simply did not leave any physical remains.
rows.translation: 这条走廊里发生了激烈的战斗；家具和碎石被堆成了临时设置的路障，但最终这些路障还是被突破了。古老的砖石墙面上布满了深深的裂痕和凹槽，显然是一些巨大的爪子把墙上的砖块撕扯下来的。在防御者的尸体旁，地上散落着几支箭头，那些箭杆早已腐烂不堪；令人不安的是，要么是攻击者表现得极为高效，以至于没有遭受任何损失，要么就是他们根本没有留下任何实物痕迹。
rows.raw: "\n        Heavy fighting took place in this hallway; furniture and rubble have been piled up into makeshift barricades that were eventually overrun. Deep gashes and gouges mark the old masonry walls, angular chunks torn out by great claws of some kind. Several arrowheads remain scattered on the floor amidst the bodies of the defenders, shafts rotted away long ago; one notices to one's unsettling dismay that the attackers were either so effective as to not suffer a single loss, or they simply did not leave any physical remains."

rows.original:
A side room leading off from your grand hall that will, in the centuries to come, become [wayfort.hasFarrah
            |Farrah's Euphoric Emporium
            |a material storeroom
        ]. In this frozen reflection of the Wayfort's past, though, it's a makeshift morgue; a heavy herbal smell hangs in the air, thick and medicinal. Distracting, but no doubt preferable to the smell of rot.
        
        At least none of the bodies are out in the open, save for one unlucky shrouded soul on the slab. A myriad of cubbyholes line two walls, bodies stacked upon each other like... well, probably the best not to think about it. For such measures to be required, the Wayfort garrison must have been taking terrible losses towards the end. That being said, given that they're all unmarked, finding any particular one would be a terrible task.
        
        Come to think of it, where did all of this go by the time you took possession of the Wayfort? The dimensions of the room are the same, but there's nothing but blank, solid walls where the bodies are being stored now. A discrepancy... maybe it's better that way, you really don't want to consider the morbid possibilities present in [wayfort.hasFarrah
            |Farrah's little shop
            |your storeroom
        ].
rows.translation:
从你的大厅延伸出来的一间侧室，在未来的几个世纪里，将会[wayfort.hasFarrah
            |法拉的欢乐商店
            |材料储藏室
        ]然而，在这个凝固了荒废驿堡过去痕迹的地方，这里其实成了一个临时停尸房；空气中弥漫着浓重的草药气味，那种味道既刺鼻又带有药味。虽然有些扰人，但比起腐烂的气味来说，无疑还是要好一些。
        
        至少，除了那具被裹在寿衣里的不幸尸体外，其他的尸体都没有被暴露在空气中。两面墙上排列着无数小隔间，那些尸体一层层堆叠在一起……嗯，最好最好不要去想这个场景。既然需要采取这样的措施，那么在战争接近尾声时，荒废驿堡驻军肯定遭受了惨重的损失。话虽如此，由于这些物品都没有任何标记，要想找到其中某一件确实是一件极其困难的任务。
        
        仔细想想，在你取得荒废驿堡的控制权之后，所有这些物品都去哪儿了呢？房间的尺寸并没有改变，但现在存放那些物品的地方却只是一面面空荡荡的墙壁而已。这种矛盾……或许这样反而更好，你真的没必要去考虑其中那些令人不寒而栗的可能性。 [wayfort.hasFarrah
            |法拉的小商店
            |你的储藏室
        ]。

rows.original:
A plinth by the old throne room — this must be the waypoint statue, or rather its equivalent in this warped reflection of the Wayfort you know. While the lupine statue is in better condition than what you remember finding it in when you first discovered the Wayfort, there's no gem: the socket is as empty as can be.

        Not that it matters. You don't think you'd be able to leave even if the statue had been whole.
rows.translation:
在古老的王座室旁有一座基座——这应该就是那个路标雕像了，或者说，是这个被扭曲的“荒废驿堡”世界中所对应的那个雕像。虽然这座雕像的状况比你最初发现“荒废驿堡”时看到的要好，但它里面并没有宝石：那个宝石镶嵌的位置空空如也。

        不过，这也没关系。你认为，即使雕像完好无损，你也不一定能离开这里吧。
rows.raw:
"
        A plinth by the old throne room — this must be the waypoint statue, or rather its equivalent in this warped reflection of the Wayfort you know. While the lupine statue is in better condition than what you remember finding it in when you first discovered the Wayfort, there's no gem: the socket is as empty as can be.

        Not that it matters. You don't think you'd be able to leave even if the statue had been whole."

rows.original:
The watchtower... yes, this is it. Even if the walls joining it to the main keep haven't completely fallen apart the way they had when you found the Wayfort, its shape is still recognizable for what it is. Desiccated, yellowed bones litter the crumbling crenellations, lending a suitably grim air to this edge of madness.

        The inside is home to a different sort of death: the remnants of an archive. Books and scrolls lie suspended in mid-air, half-torn as they're thrown off their shelves by some terrible force; the shelves and bookcases themselves are frozen in the process of collapsing, presumably crushed by the same power. Even the staircase to the watchtower's upper reaches has been shattered, chunks of old masonry looming ominously over you, poised to fall but never actually making the descent.
        
        Despite the chaos, the rest of the interior is unharmed — a standing desk, an old spyglass in a display case, and even the summoning circle is still there along with the interior walls. Presumably that's why it survived to this day for you to find it intact...
rows.translation:
那座瞭望塔……没错，就是它。虽然将它与主城堡连接起来的墙壁并没有像你发现荒废驿堡时那样彻底坍塌，但它的形状依然可以被辨认出来。干枯、发黄的骨头散落在那些摇摇欲坠的垛口上，为这片充满疯狂与荒凉的地方增添了一丝阴森的气氛。

        这里蕴含着另一种形式的“死亡”：一个档案馆的残余。书籍和卷轴悬在半空中，被某种强大的力量从书架上抛落下来，导致它们半毁不全；书架和书柜本身也在倒塌的过程中被毁，想必也是被同样的力量压垮的。就连通往瞭望塔高层的楼梯也已经被毁坏，那些古老的砖石碎片悬在上方，看起来随时都会掉落，但实际上却始终没有坠下来。
        
        尽管一片混乱，但塔内的其他部分却完好无损——那里有一张可移动的书桌，一个陈列在展柜里的旧望远镜，甚至连那个召唤阵和内墙也都还在原处。大概正是因为这个原因，它才得以保存至今，让你能够完好无损地找到它……

"
        The watchtower... yes, this is it. Even if the walls joining it to the main keep haven't completely fallen apart the way they had when you found the Wayfort, its shape is still recognizable for what it is.         The inside is home to a different sort of death: the remnants of an archive. Even the staircase to the watchtower's upper reaches has been shattered, chunks of old masonry looming ominously over you, poised to fall but never actually making the descent.
        
        Despite the chaos, the rest of the interior is unharmed — a standing desk, an old spyglass in a display case, and even the summoning circle is still there along with the interior walls. Presumably that's why it survived to this day for you to find it intact..."

rows.original:
A twisted version of the familiar bridge that spans the River Ridell — the structure itself is still serviceable, but the viscous liquid that flows beneath it is most certainly not water. As you traverse its length, it warps and folds back upon itself, the slight tilt of the bridge's plane the only hint that something's amiss until one looks up to find bridge and water above as well as below. Or is that right, given that up and down don't exist here?

        The smooth, oily sound of liquid as it rushes past stone supports... you're not sure if there's anything alive in the so-called water as you continue to pace down the bridge, but you can't shake the sense that there're multiple things watching you from inside the water. Or maybe, just maybe, the water itself is watching you...
rows.translation:
这是那座横跨里德尔河的熟悉桥梁的扭曲版本——桥梁本身依然可以正常使用，但流经其下方的粘稠液体绝对不是水。当你走过这座桥时，它会不断扭曲、折叠，而桥梁平面的轻微倾斜才是唯一能暗示出异常存在的迹象。直到你抬头望去，才会发现桥的上方和下方都流淌着同样的粘稠液体。或者，既然在这里根本不存在上下之分，这种想法本身也就不成立了吧？

        当液体从石壁上流过时，会发出那种平滑而黏腻的声音……当你继续沿着桥面前行时，你其实并不确定所谓的“水中”是否真的有什么生物存在，但你就是有一种感觉——似乎有无数东西正在水中注视着你。或者，仅仅只是也许，水本身正在注视着你……
rows.raw:
"
        A twisted version of the familiar bridge that spans the River Ridell — the structure itself is still serviceable, but the viscous liquid that flows beneath it is most certainly not water. As you traverse its length, it warps and folds back upon itself, the slight tilt of the bridge's plane the only hint that something's amiss until one looks up to find bridge and water above as well as below. Or is that right, given that up and down don't exist here?

        The smooth, oily sound of liquid as it rushes past stone supports... you're not sure if there's anything alive in the so-called water as you continue to pace down the bridge, but you can't shake the sense that there're multiple things watching you from inside the water. Or maybe, just maybe, the water itself is watching you..."

rows.original:
The main grounds of the Wayfort sprawl out around you, covered in debris and stained with old blood. The remains of the fallen lie amidst the rubble, although you're careful to not take too close a look at them lest you see something more unsettling than what you have already... of course, getting here made no sense to begin with, what with you traveling from the main keep over the bridge to the courtyard when it should've been the other way around.

        And of course, the boulder — you remember there being one right in the courtyard's center when you first entered the Wayfort, a huge chunk of rock you had to have removed. This specimen, though, is much larger and more imposing than you remember; its glossy black and gleaming facets are certainly a figment of this place rather than the old boring rock you remember in reality.
rows.translation:
荒废驿堡的主要区域就展现在你周围，到处都是碎片，还残留着陈旧的血液痕迹。那些倒下的人的残骸就埋在废墟之中，不过你得小心谨慎，不要靠得太近去看，否则你可能会看到一些比你已经看到的更加令人不安的东西。当然，一开始就觉得来到这里根本毫无意义——你本应该从主城堡穿过桥来到庭院，但实际上却反过来了。

        还有那块巨石——你应该还记得，当你第一次进入荒废驿堡时，庭院的正中央就有一块巨大的岩石，你必须把它移开才行。然而，这个样本实际上要比你记忆中的大得多，也更加壮观；它那光亮的黑色表面以及闪烁的光芒，显然更符合这个地方的特点，而不是你现实中所记得的那种古老而乏味的岩石。
rows.raw:
"
        The main grounds of the Wayfort sprawl out around you, covered in debris and stained with old blood. The remains of the fallen lie amidst the rubble, although you're careful to not take too close a look at them lest you see something more unsettling than what you have already... of course, getting here made no sense to begin with, what with you traveling from the main keep over the bridge to the courtyard when it should've been the other way around.

        And of course, the boulder — you remember there being one right in the courtyard's center when you first entered the Wayfort, a huge chunk of rock you had to have removed. This specimen, though, is much larger and more imposing than you remember; its glossy black and gleaming facets are certainly a figment of this place rather than the old boring rock you remember in reality."

rows.original:
You're standing on the southern bank of a small, placid lake nestled between three stony hills. There's a small valley running north from here, through which water flows into the Undermountain. You also see the rubble from ancient aqueducts here, remnants of Khor'minos's engineering prowess left to crumble with the passage of time. They once serviced the town of Hawkethorne centuries ago, but you doubt anyone's drawn water except from the well in town for a hundred years or more now.

        Just north of here, there's a precipitous overhang of stone looming across the narrow path by the waterside. Best tread lightly.
rows.translation:
你站在一片宁静的小湖的南岸，这片湖泊被三座岩石山丘环绕着。从这里向北延伸，有一条小山谷，河水便是通过这条山谷流入地下山脉的。你还能看到这里残留的古老引水渠的废墟，这些都是科尔米诺斯在工程学方面的卓越成就的见证，只是随着时间的流逝，它们已经逐渐损毁、变得支离破碎了。几个世纪前，他们曾经为鹰棘镇镇提供过服务，但可以肯定的是，在过去的百年里，除了镇上的那口井，应该没有人再从其他地方取水了。

        就在这里以北，沿着水边的狭窄小路，有一处陡峭的石壁耸立在道路上。最好谨慎行事。
rows.raw:
"
        You're standing on the southern bank of a small, placid lake nestled between three stony hills. There's a small valley running north from here, through which water flows into the Undermountain. You also see the rubble from ancient aqueducts here, remnants of Khor'minos's engineering prowess left to crumble with the passage of time. They once serviced the town of Hawkethorne centuries ago, but you doubt anyone's drawn water except from the well in town for a hundred years or more now.

        Just north of here, there's a precipitous overhang of stone looming across the narrow path by the waterside. Best tread lightly."

rows.original:
You're standing under a precarious-looking overhang of stone, jutting from the hillside to loom over the waterhead now to your east. It might make for a great diving spot, honestly, if you're sure the water's deep enough to cushion the fall. 

        There's a narrow path around the side of the lake here, heading north towards the mountains, or south towards... well, nothing really, but that's how you got here. The climb back's going to be an ass-pain isn't it?
rows.translation:
你正站在一处看起来相当危险的石质悬岩下，这块岩石从山坡上延伸出来，如今正好俯瞰着你东边的水域。说实话，如果确定水深足够缓冲坠落的冲击力，这里倒是个不错的跳水地点。

        湖边有一条狭窄的小路，可以往北通往山区，或者往南延伸……嗯，其实南边并没有什么特别的景点，但你就是沿着这条路来到这里的。不过，要爬回去的话，肯定会非常辛苦吧？
rows.raw:
"
        You're standing under a precarious-looking overhang of stone, jutting from the hillside to loom over the waterhead now to your east. It might make for a great diving spot, honestly, if you're sure the water's deep enough to cushion the fall. 

        There's a narrow path around the side of the lake here, heading north towards the mountains, or south towards... well, nothing really, but that's how you got here. The climb back's going to be an ass-pain isn't it?"

rows.original:
From the waterhead, a deep but relatively narrow river is running downslope towards what you can now definitively see is a cave entrance — an entrance to the beleaguered Kingdom of Khor'minos, if indirectly. There's a thin path along the water's edge for you to follow, rocky and uneven but sturdy enough to support even Livrea's weight comfortably. 

        There's a small wood bridge crossing the river just up ahead. 
        
        There's a small gully northeast of here, cut from the side of the hill by the thunder of water pouring down from it to join the waterhead. You can see smoke rising from it...
rows.translation:
从源头开始，一条深而狭窄的河流顺着山坡向下流淌，最终汇入一个洞穴入口——虽然这条河流是间接地通向了那座陷入困境的科尔米诺斯王国的。沿着河岸有一条狭窄的小路可供通行，这条小路由岩石构成，路面崎岖不平，但足以承受莉维娅的体重，让人行走起来十分舒适。 

        在前方不远处，有一座横跨河流的小木桥。
        
        在这座桥的东北方向，有一条小沟壑。它是由于山上的水流湍急而下，冲刷出山体侧面而形成的，最终这些水流会汇入河流的主流。你可以看到那里有烟雾升起……
rows.raw:
"
        From the waterhead, a deep but relatively narrow river is running downslope towards what you can now definitively see is a cave entrance — an entrance to the beleaguered Kingdom of Khor'minos, if indirectly. There's a thin path along the water's edge for you to follow, rocky and uneven but sturdy enough to support even Livrea's weight comfortably. 

        There's a small wood bridge crossing the river just up ahead. 
        
        There's a small gully northeast of here, cut from the side of the hill by the thunder of water pouring down from it to join the waterhead. You can see smoke rising from it..."

rows.original: From the waterhead, a deep but relatively narrow river is running downslope towards what might be a cave entrance — an entrance to the beleaguered Kingdom of Khor'minos! There's a thin path along the water's edge for you to follow, rocky and uneven but sturdy enough to support even Livrea's weight comfortably.
rows.translation: 从源头开始，一条深而狭窄的河流顺着山坡向下流淌，最终似乎通向一个洞穴入口——那可能是通往陷入困境的科尔米诺斯王国的入口！沿着河岸有一条狭窄的小路可供你行走，这条小路虽然多岩石且不平坦，但足够结实，甚至能够轻松承载莉维娅的体重。
rows.raw: "\n        From the waterhead, a deep but relatively narrow river is running downslope towards what might be a cave entrance — an entrance to the beleaguered Kingdom of Khor'minos! There's a thin path along the water's edge for you to follow, rocky and uneven but sturdy enough to support even Livrea's weight comfortably."

rows.original:
With the kobolds scattered in terror, you can now see that you're standing in a crossroads of sorts...

        To the north is the yawning, shadowed entrance to the cave the little lizards were so keen on guarding. 
        
        To the immediate east, across a narrow, ramshackle foot bridge, is a small camp they were living in. There's still a cookfire going, and their tents have been left behind.
        
        Back south, you can follow the river to the waterhead, though that's the way you came. Not much back that way now.
rows.translation:
那些被恐惧驱散的狗头人们，让你清楚地看到自己此刻正站在一个十字路口……

        向北走去，就是那条被阴影笼罩的洞穴入口——那些小蜥蜴们曾经如此拼命地想要守护它。 
        
        在正东方向，穿过一座狭窄而破旧的步行桥，就是他们当时居住的小营地。那里的篝火依然在燃烧，他们的帐篷也被留在了那里。
        
        如果往南走，沿着河流就能找到水源地，不过那也是你来的时候走过的路线。现在那边已经没什么人了。
rows.raw:
"
        With the kobolds scattered in terror, you can now see that you're standing in a crossroads of sorts...

        To the north is the yawning, shadowed entrance to the cave the little lizards were so keen on guarding. 
        
        To the immediate east, across a narrow, ramshackle foot bridge, is a small camp they were living in. There's still a cookfire going, and their tents have been left behind.
        
        Back south, you can follow the river to the waterhead, though that's the way you came. Not much back that way now."

rows.original: Across the river from the path you've been taking is a small grotto, in which the kobolds have pitched their camp. It's hardly an impressive thing, just a few huddled tents and a meager fire pit. Without their tending it, the rat meat skewered over the flames has gone black. You doubt the kobolds have anything of value here, but it is safe from the wind and sun here.
rows.translation: 在你一直走过的那条小路上方，河对岸有一个小洞穴，那些狗头人就在那里扎营。那里其实没什么特别的，只不过是一些挤在一起搭建的帐篷，以及一个简陋的火堆而已。由于没有人照料，那些架在火上的老鼠肉早就烤黑了。你怀疑狗头人们在那里并没有什么值钱的东西，但至少这个地方可以避风避日。
rows.raw: "\n        Across the river from the path you've been taking is a small grotto, in which the kobolds have pitched their camp. It's hardly an impressive thing, just a few huddled tents and a meager fire pit. Without their tending it, the rat meat skewered over the flames has gone black. You doubt the kobolds have anything of value here, but it is safe from the wind and sun here."

rows.original:
You're standing in the entrance to a pitch-black cave. It's cold as ice inside, and the sound of the river rushing past is almost deafening. Livrea gives you a nervous glance, putting her hand on the hilt of her sword. 

        North will take you inside, into the dark.
        
        South will return you to the light where you belong.
rows.translation:
你站在一个漆黑洞穴的入口处。洞内寒气刺骨，河流奔流的声音几乎震耳欲聋。莉维娅紧张地看了你一眼，然后将手放在剑柄上。

        向北走，你将进入暗影之中。
        
        向南走，你将回到属于你的光明之中。
rows.raw:
"
        You're standing in the entrance to a pitch-black cave. It's cold as ice inside, and the sound of the river rushing past is almost deafening. Livrea gives you a nervous glance, putting her hand on the hilt of her sword. 

        North will take you inside, into the dark.
        
        South will return you to the light where you belong."

rows.original:
You're deep inside a cold, dark cave underneath the great mountains that house Khor'minos. A river is rushing to the northwest along a downwards slope... but from that direction is also coming a tremendous snarling sound, like some titanic beast baring its fangs.

        Livrea's glancing towards a narrower branch of the cave that least away from the water, heading due east. It's barely big enough for the bard to get through without ducking her head, and she might have some trouble squeezing her bust through there, but it's better than the alternative... right?
rows.translation:
你此刻身处科尔米诺斯山脉下方的一处寒冷而暗影的洞穴之中。有一条河流沿着向下倾斜的地势向西北方向奔流而去……但正是从那个方向传来了震耳欲聋的咆哮声，仿佛有某种巨大的野兽正在露出獠牙。

        莉维娅指向洞穴中一条离水面最近的狭窄通道，那条通道正好能让人从那里穿过，不过诗人必须低下头才行；她的胸部可能会有些困难才能挤过去，但总比其他选择要好。对吧？
rows.raw:
"
        You're deep inside a cold, dark cave underneath the great mountains that house Khor'minos. A river is rushing to the northwest along a downwards slope... but from that direction is also coming a tremendous snarling sound, like some titanic beast baring its fangs.

        Livrea's glancing towards a narrower branch of the cave that least away from the water, heading due east. It's barely big enough for the bard to get through without ducking her head, and she might have some trouble squeezing her bust through there, but it's better than the alternative... right?"

rows.original: The thunderous noise of snarling is even louder here, almost enough to overshadow the roar of the river pouring down into the Undermountain. Beast bones are scattered around haphazardly, piled against the walls or crushed underfoot by something large and very, very heavy. Going further north will no doubt bring you face to face with the source of this carnage. Unfortunately, that's the way this river's running. Back south is the branch in the cave.
rows.translation: 这里，那些低吼声带来的震耳欲聋的噪音更为剧烈，几乎足以盖过那些倾泻而下、汇入地下山脉的河流的咆哮声。野兽的骨头散落在各处，有的随意堆放在墙边，有的则被某些庞大而重型的东西踩得粉碎。 继续向北前进，你无疑会遇到这场屠杀的根源。不幸的是，这条河就是这样的流向。 往南走，就能找到洞穴里的那条支流。
rows.raw: " The thunderous noise of snarling is even louder here, almost enough to overshadow the roar of the river pouring down into the Undermountain. Beast bones are scattered around haphazardly, piled against the walls or crushed underfoot by something large and very, very heavy. Going further north will no doubt bring you face to face with the source of this carnage. Unfortunately, that's the way this river's running. Back south is the branch in the cave."

rows.original:
You're squeezing into a very narrow cavern passage branched off from the main tunnel. You doubt whatever tremendous beast is making all that racket could fit through here, and there's no signs of the kobolds having entered either. You might well be the first person to come through here in centuries.

        The tunnel widens again to the east. 
        
        Back south is the junction and river.
rows.translation:
你正挤进一条从主隧道分支出来的狭窄洞穴通道。你怀疑，那种制造出如此巨大声响的庞然大物根本不可能通过这里，而且也没有任何迹象表明狗头人们曾经进入过这里。很可能你是几个世纪以来第一个穿过这条通道的人。

        向东走，隧道又变宽了。
        
        再往南走，就会来到岔路口和那条河流。
rows.raw:
"
        You're squeezing into a very narrow cavern passage branched off from the main tunnel. You doubt whatever tremendous beast is making all that racket could fit through here, and there's no signs of the kobolds having entered either. You might well be the first person to come through here in centuries.

        The tunnel widens again to the east. 
        
        Back south is the junction and river."

rows.original:
The cave here is a little wider than it was back to the west, where you came from, though it's still so narrow that you can only walk single-file through the cave. Liv's grumbling quietly behind you — every couple of steps, she's bonking one of her horns on some outcropping of rock or another. 

        There seems to be a branch up ahead to the east, widening out a bit to either side.
rows.translation:
这里的洞穴比你从西边来的那段要宽一些，不过依然狭窄到只能让人们排成一列才能通过。莉芙在你身后不停地抱怨着——每隔几步，她就会用她的角去撞那些突出的岩石。

        前面似乎有一条通往东边的岔路，道路的两侧稍微宽了一些。
rows.raw:
"
        The cave here is a little wider than it was back to the west, where you came from, though it's still so narrow that you can only walk single-file through the cave. Liv's grumbling quietly behind you — every couple of steps, she's bonking one of her horns on some outcropping of rock or another. 

        There seems to be a branch up ahead to the east, widening out a bit to either side."

rows.original:
The end of this branch cave splits again. To the north, there's a pretty steep incline, from whence you can hear that same terrible snarling noise as from before. Does this loop back around to the monster's den? 

        To the south, though, is another branch that seems... oddly quiet and still. There's a few strips of cloth scattered around the entrance, and what looks like half of a bronze shield is wedged into a narrow crack in the wall. Maybe somebody has been this way in recent years? No, no, these look just as old as the ruins outside. Ancient, but not terribly weathered by the passing of years...
rows.translation:
这个支洞的尽头又分出了另一条通道。向北走，会遇到一段相当陡峭的坡道，从那里可以听到之前那种可怕的咆哮声——难道这条通道是通向怪物巢穴的？

        不过，向南走的话，似乎还有另一条分支通道。奇怪的是，这里一片寂静无声。入口处散落着几条布条，而半块青铜盾似乎被卡在墙上的一个狭窄裂缝里。也许近年来有人来过这里吧？不，不，这些看起来和外面的废墟一样古老。虽然年代久远，但并没有因为岁月的流逝而受到太大的侵蚀……
rows.raw:
"
        The end of this branch cave splits again. To the north, there's a pretty steep incline, from whence you can hear that same terrible snarling noise as from before. Does this loop back around to the monster's den? 

        To the south, though, is another branch that seems... oddly quiet and still. There's a few strips of cloth scattered around the entrance, and what looks like half of a bronze shield is wedged into a narrow crack in the wall. Maybe somebody has been this way in recent years? No, no, these look just as old as the ruins outside. Ancient, but not terribly weathered by the passing of years..."

rows.original: You're standing on a small outcropping of rock overlooking the lair of the sea wyrm. The beast is still snoozing, blissfully unaware of your presence, though its snoring is loud enough to make your teeth ache. The reverberations off the cave wall are deafening, and on the deepest of its noises, bits of rock are shaken loose from the walls and go tumbling down into its little nest. From your vantage point here, you can see that there's a particularly large stalactite on the ceiling of the chamber the wyrm's roosting in. One good blast and it might just come loose, but the rocks here are so unstable that the gods only know what kind of mayhem the impact of it crashing down would unleash.
rows.translation: 你站在一块小岩石上，俯瞰着那条海怪的巢穴。那只怪物仍在沉睡，完全没有察觉到你的存在，不过它的鼾声大得足以让你的牙齿都感到疼痛。那些震动在洞穴的墙壁上回荡，震耳欲聋；而在它鼾声最剧烈的时候，甚至有一些岩石会从墙壁上脱落，掉进它的巢穴里。 从你现在的位置来看，你可以清楚地看到在那个巨龙栖息的洞室里，天花板上有一根特别大的钟乳石。只要用尽全力敲击一下，那些岩石或许就会松动下来，但这里的岩石实在太不稳定了，天知道它们坠落下来会引发什么样的灾难。
rows.raw: " You're standing on a small outcropping of rock overlooking the lair of the sea wyrm. The beast is still snoozing, blissfully unaware of your presence, though its snoring is loud enough to make your teeth ache. The reverberations off the cave wall are deafening, and on the deepest of its noises, bits of rock are shaken loose from the walls and go tumbling down into its little nest. From your vantage point here, you can see that there's a particularly large stalactite on the ceiling of the chamber the wyrm's roosting in. One good blast and it might just come loose, but the rocks here are so unstable that the gods only know what kind of mayhem the impact of it crashing down would unleash."

rows.original:
According to Livrea, this appears to have been the camp of some Belharan soldiers during the Godswar, perhaps finding shelter from the ravages of battle outside... or whatever cataclysm destroyed the old city of Hawkethorne. 

        There are scattered remnants of military equipment, but it's all rusted out or shattered beyond repair. You've already taken everything worth carrying out of this place[flags.LQ1_CHEST||, save for the contents of that locked chest sitting in the back]. There's no evidence of bodies here, at least. You doubt whatever ancient warriors that sheltered here made this their last stand.
        
        The only exit is back north, the way you came.
rows.translation:
据莉维娅所说，这里似乎曾是某些贝拉兰士兵在神战期间的营地——他们或许是为了躲避战火带来的破坏，或是为了躲避那场摧毁了鹰棘镇古城的灾难而来到这里的。

        现场散落着一些军事装备的残骸，但它们都已经生锈变形，或者碎得无法修复了。你们已经把所有值得带走的东西都从这里带走了。[flags.LQ1_CHEST||除了放在后面的那个上锁的箱子里的东西之外，其他的都还完好无损。]至少，这里并没有发现任何尸体的痕迹。你怀疑那些曾经在这里避难的古战士们，是否真的将这里作为他们的最后防线。
        
        唯一的出口就是往北返回，也就是你来的那条路。
rows.raw:
"
        According to Livrea, this appears to have been the camp of some Belharan soldiers during the Godswar, perhaps finding shelter from the ravages of battle outside... or whatever cataclysm destroyed the old city of Hawkethorne. 

        There are scattered remnants of military equipment, but it's all rusted out or shattered beyond repair. You've already taken everything worth carrying out of this place[flags.LQ1_CHEST||, save for the contents of that locked chest sitting in the back]. There's no evidence of bodies here, at least. You doubt whatever ancient warriors that sheltered here made this their last stand.
        
        The only exit is back north, the way you came."

rows.original: This is your house! You've only had it for about a year, but it's finally starting to look like a home. The wood bed your father helped you carve is still the most prominent fixture, but you've begun adding small things to make it your own. A small ancestral shrine you crafted yourself sits opposite the bed, and a small half-desk with an oil lamp rounds out the decor. There are other things, of course, but overall you can't shake the feeling that it just isn't the same as living with people. Perhaps it's the size of the place...
rows.translation: 这就是你的家了！虽然你才住了一年左右，但它终于开始变得像一个真正的家了。你父亲帮忙你制作的木床依然是家里最显眼的摆设，而你也开始添置一些小物件，让它真正成为属于你的家。你亲手制作的一个小祖宗神龛放在床的对面，还有一个配着油灯的小半张书桌，这些构成了整个装饰风格。当然，还有其他一些小物件，但总体来说，你还是会觉得，这样的生活与和别人一起生活是不一样的。也许是因为这个地方的大小吧……
rows.raw: "This is your house! You've only had it for about a year, but it's finally starting to look like a home. The wood bed your father helped you carve is still the most prominent fixture, but you've begun adding small things to make it your own. A small ancestral shrine you crafted yourself sits opposite the bed, and a small half-desk with an oil lamp rounds out the decor. There are other things, of course, but overall you can't shake the feeling that it just isn't the same as living with people. Perhaps it's the size of the place..."

rows.original: The village is mostly empty at the moment. People will be congregating at the ritual circle, so there won't be anyone in any of the huts at the moment. They range in size from single person homes to the great long-house where town meetings are held and travelers set up shop. Fewer and fewer merchants have been showing up since the start of the great war, and the most recent ones have been fleeing for unknown places further southwest. Nothing overly dangerous has come over the mountains, but it's still been a pall over the village.
rows.translation: 目前这个村庄基本上空无一人。人们都会聚集在仪式圈那里，所以此刻这些小屋里根本没有人。这些小屋的大小各不相同，有的只够一个人居住，而有的则是那种用来举行镇民会议或供旅行者暂住的长屋。自从这场大战爆发以来，出现的商贩越来越少了，而最近那些来的商贩也都纷纷逃往了西南方向的一些未知地区。虽然并没有什么特别危险的东西从山区传过来，但这种气氛依然让整个村庄笼罩在一片阴郁之中。

rows.original: Your parents' house! It still feels like home, even though you've been gone for a while. The bedding you slept in has been repurposed for extra warmth during the chillier months, and every ounce of usable space feels used. Somehow, despite that, it doesn't feel cluttered. You return often, visiting for anything ranging from meals to simply hanging out. It's easily twice the size of your own home, the perfect place to raise a family.
rows.translation: 你父母的房子！即使你已经离开有一段时间了，那里依然让人感觉像家一样温馨。你曾经睡过的被褥在寒冷的季节被重新利用起来，为房间增添了更多的温暖，而每一个可利用的空间似乎都被充分利用了。不过，奇怪的是，那里一点也不显得杂乱。你经常回去探望，无论是为了吃饭还是只是随便闲逛。那房子的面积几乎是你们自己家的两倍，真的是养育家庭的理想之地。
rows.raw: "Your parents' house! It still feels like home, even though you've been gone for a while. The bedding you slept in has been repurposed for extra warmth during the chillier months, and every ounce of usable space feels used. Somehow, despite that, it doesn't feel cluttered. You return often, visiting for anything ranging from meals to simply hanging out. It's easily twice the size of your own home, the perfect place to raise a family."

rows.original: This section of the village begins the path out to the ritual grounds. Just because nothing bad has come yet, doesn't mean there won't be any problems later. That's why the ritual needs to work. [flags.ATUGIA_QUEST_MOM||You wouldn't be caught dead at the ritual with half finished markings. Get help before heading out there!]
rows.translation: 村庄的这一段道路通向祭祀场地。仅仅因为目前还没有发生任何不好的事情，并不意味着以后就不会出现问题。因此，这个祭祀仪式必须能够发挥作用。 [flags.ATUGIA_QUEST_MOM||如果你在仪式上进行标记时只完成了一半，绝对会出大麻烦的。在去之前赶紧找人帮忙吧！]
rows.raw: "This section of the village begins the path out to the ritual grounds. Just because nothing bad has come yet, doesn't mean there won't be any problems later. That's why the ritual needs to work.\n \n [flags.ATUGIA_QUEST_MOM||You wouldn't be caught dead at the ritual with half finished markings. Get help before heading out there!]"

rows.original: The further from the center of the village one gets, the less numerous homes become. Things are just too close-knit for even the loners to get too far from each other. There are a couple people who need their space, but even their homes are empty now. No one wants to skimp out on aiding the elders in calling forth a force worthy of protecting us from any threats that come even close to the village.
rows.translation: 离村庄中心越远，房屋的数量就越少。这里的人们关系太过紧密，就连那些喜欢独来独往的人也不愿意离其他人太远。虽然有那么几个人需要一些私人空间，但他们的房子现在也都空着。没有人愿意不愿意帮忙老人们召唤出一种力量，来保护我们免受任何可能接近村庄的威胁。
rows.raw: "The further from the center of the village one gets, the less numerous homes become. Things are just too close-knit for even the loners to get too far from each other. There are a couple people who need their space, but even their homes are empty now. No one wants to skimp out on aiding the elders in calling forth a force worthy of protecting us from any threats that come even close to the village."

rows.original: Out this far there aren't any homes, and usually there aren't many traces of life in general. Ritual circles for varying degrees of ancestral contact and guidance are scattered about the fields that stretch close to the mountains. Some of them are so small that they would be invisible to someone who didn't know what they were looking for. At the largest, the rest of the village has gathered to begin channeling the combined power of the village ancestors.
rows.translation: 在这片区域之外，根本没有任何房屋，通常也看不到多少生命的痕迹。在那些延伸至山脚的田野里，分布着一些用于与祖先建立联系、寻求指引的仪式场所。其中一些仪式圈规模非常小，如果不知道在寻找什么的话，根本无法发现它们的存在。而在规模最大的那些仪式场所，整个村庄的居民都会聚集过来，共同调动全村祖先的力量。
rows.raw: "Out this far there aren't any homes, and usually there aren't many traces of life in general. Ritual circles for varying degrees of ancestral contact and guidance are scattered about the fields that stretch close to the mountains. Some of them are so small that they would be invisible to someone who didn't know what they were looking for. At the largest, the rest of the village has gathered to begin channeling the combined power of the village ancestors."
