rows.translation: 摘自贾勒萨·蒂里·阿斯特里德·冈瓦尔德森所著的《埃斯特洛尔的神秘秘籍：一个局外人的视角》。
rows.raw: ' From "The Grand Arcana of Estelore: An Outsider's Perspective" by Jarlessa Thyri Astrid Gunvaldsen. '

rows.original: The first recorded practitioners of what we would call magic were tribal shamans, who passed their little-understood hedgecraft down through a well developed oral tradition. With each successive generation, the chaotic magics of these shamans was explored ever more deeply, slowly refined through trial and error and experimentation across uncounted centuries. I can only imagine how many shamans were lost to wild, consumptive magic escaping their control as they fumbled in the dark for a greater understanding of that deadly ancestral arts. When the great dragons of Aerimarne taught their dragonclaw script to the early Belharans, it is said that High King Ramius's first command was that his shamans and oracles use the new script to impress the syllables that made up their words of power into clay, so that their knowledge could be distributed across his kingdom. Thus, the first spellbooks were created — or spell tablets, more accurately, but the point stands: from then on, magic became standardized, the knowledge spread in a web of magical mastery across the early empire. Soon, any scholar capable of reading the dragonmarks was allowed to learn spellcraft, rather than an art only taught between shamanic master and apprentices. My contemporaries in the grand academy of Estelore attribute this royal decree with beginning Belhar's rise to power, and there is likely some grain of truth to that belief; certainly, Belhar has the largest and most well-developed cadre of magisters the world has ever seen at its command, from the Spellblades of Maidenbridge to the Mage-Priests of Nareva to the Arch-magisters of Estelore. The patronage of Belhar's emperors has allowed magic to evolve from hedgecraft and superstition to a topic of research as accessible as history or economics. Even the distant priest-kings of Kitsuhon cannot match the empire for its peerless mastery of the arcane. But, my dear reader, what is it that these vaunted magisters study today? The college of Estelore defines a spell, the archetypal example of magic used in the world, thusly: "Any conscious, controlled invocation of aetheric energy channeled into a repeatable, predictable shape." Spellcraft is at the heart of anyone's understanding of magic, as it is how we interact with magic. To craft a spell, a would-be magister needs three things: the first is knowledge. Spells are memorized, ritual invocations that make use of specific words of power, ancient draconic syllables chanted in specific orders that prime the ambient aetheric energy around the caster. These words must be spoken forcefully and clearly, as a single misspoken phrase can change the nature of the spell, twisting it out of the caster's control. This is why a catalyst of some kind is necessary to safely cast a spell: should a spell go wild and awry, it is possible to focus the backlash into a treated arcane object and away from the caster. Without a catalyst, the discharged wild magic will have nowhere to go but the caster. Lastly, a mage needs force of will. The aether is inherently entropic, and left to its own devices does nothing; through the words of power, a mage can shape magic to her will, but it requires a great force of will to discharge the spell. This execution is also commensurately draining; more powerful spells require greater experience and will to cast, and sap more strength from the mage in the casting. I have more than once now mentioned wild magic. Perhaps it is time to address that most dangerous mammoth in the barn. A misspoken word of power, or a lack of sufficient will to execute a spell, can cause magic to slip out of the caster's control. Aetheric energy inherently wishes to be discharged — keeping a spell going for more than a momentary invocation demands a great deal of focused concentration, and artifacts that constantly channel magic are rare wonders indeed. Without a proper outlet (ie., a spell), the magical energy will discharge itself in what thus far scholars have conceded appears to be entirely random ways. The unfortunate caster often ends up acting as a lightning rod, attracting the power of the foiled spell back into herself, with predictably disastrous consequences — brain hemorrhage, uncontrolled mutation, or even spontaneous combustions are among the effects I have myself witnessed befall other mages. This is, again, why we carry catalysts, as a treated arcane crystal apparently acts as a more tempting target for wild magic to discharge into; and believe me, you would rather have an expensive wand shatter in your hand than have your brain liquify out of your nose. When controlled properly, however, magic is generally fairly predictable. When you invoke the spell Fireball, every time you cast the spell a ball of fire will lance out from your palm and detonate at a point you aimed at, arcing much like a loosed arrow, and washing over a radius of some twenty feet. You may not always get the results you want — just because you throw a Fireball at someone doesn't mean you'll hit them — but so long as you execute the spell correctly, it will produce reliable and repeatable effects. The college of Estelore today divides its catalog of spells into four broad categories, based on related properties. Each category, or school, has a devoted following of magisters who specialize in it, delving ever deeper into its mysteries and crafting new spells to further their specialty's prestige within the college. Their studies are downright competitive, though alas it is always the school of conjuration that is destined to win — if only because they have the monopoly on Fireballs.
rows.translation: 据记载，最早实践我们如今称之为……的人们是魔法他们是部落中的萨满，通过完善的口述传统，将这些鲜为人知的神秘技艺代代相传。随着时间的推移，每一代萨满都不断地深入探索这些混乱而神奇的魔法，通过无数次的尝试与实验，这些技艺才逐渐得到了完善。我只能想象，在那些试图更深入地理解这些古老而危险的魔法的过程中，究竟有多少萨满因为那些失控的、具有破坏性的魔力而失去了生命。 据说，当艾瑞玛恩的巨龙们将他们的龙爪文字传授给早期的贝拉人时，高王拉米乌斯的第一道命令就是让他的萨满和先知们用这种新的文字将构成他们法术词汇的音节刻在黏土上，这样他们的知识就能传播到他的整个王国中去。就这样，第一批法术书应运而生——或者更准确地说，是法术铭文石板。从那时起，魔法开始被标准化，这些知识通过魔法传承的网络在早期帝国中传播开来。不久之后，任何能够解读龙纹的人都被允许学习法术，而不再只是由萨满大师和学徒之间私下传授。 在埃斯特洛尔这座伟大的学院里，我的同龄人们认为，正是这份皇家法令开启了贝尔哈尔的权力之路，这种观点或许确实有一定道理；毫无疑问，贝尔哈尔麾下拥有迄今为止世界上规模最大、实力最强大的法师团队——从梅登布里奇的法术剑士们，到娜瑞瓦的法师祭司们，再到埃斯特洛尔的大法师们，无一不是他的得力助手。贝尔哈尔皇帝们的支持使得魔法从一种边缘技艺和迷信，发展成为一门与历史或经济学同样值得研究的学科。就连遥远的基苏洪地区的祭司国王们，也无法在魔法研究领域与这个帝国相媲美。 但是，亲爱的读者，这些备受推崇的法师们如今究竟在研究什么呢？ 埃斯特洛尔学院对法术的定义是：“任何有意识、受控制的以太能量运用，这些能量被引导成可重复、可预测的形式。”法术制作是理解魔法的根本，因为正是通过这种方式，我们才能与魔法进行互动。 要施展一个法术，一位有志成为法师的人需要三样东西：第一件就是知识法术是通过记忆来施展的，这些仪式性的召唤语需要使用特定的力量词汇，或是按照特定的顺序吟诵古老的巨龙语节，从而激发施法者周围的环境能量。这些词汇必须被清晰而有力地念出，因为哪怕一个发音错误，都可能改变法术的性质，使其脱离施法者的控制。正因如此催化剂某种媒介是安全施展法术所必需的：如果法术失控、出现异常，就可以将由此产生的反作用力引导到经过特殊处理的神秘物品上，从而避免其伤害到施法者本身。如果没有这种媒介，那些失控的魔法能量就只会冲击施法者本身。总之，法师是需要这样的工具的。意志力以太本身具有熵的特性，如果任其自然发展，什么也不会发生；而法师通过咒语的力量，能够将自己的意志赋予魔法，但释放这些咒语需要强大的意志力。这种施法过程也会消耗大量的精力——威力越强的咒语，所需的经验与意志力就越大，施法时法师消耗的能量也会越多。 我之前已经不止一次提到过“野性魔法”这个概念。或许现在是时候认真讨论一下这个游戏中最危险的元素了。一个措辞不当的法术咒语，或者执行法术时缺乏足够的意志力，都可能导致魔法失控，从而给施法者带来严重的后果。以太能量本质上具有释放的倾向——要让一个法术持续发挥作用而不仅仅是在瞬间被施展出来，就需要投入极大的专注力；而那些能够持续引导魔法能量的神器，确实堪称稀世珍宝。如果没有适当的释放途径（也就是相应的法术），这些魔法能量就会以完全随机的方式释放出来。不幸的是，施法者往往会成为这种能量的“导火索”，那些未能成功释放的法术力量会反噬到施法者身上，从而导致灾难性的后果——我亲眼见过其他法师因此出现脑出血、身体发生不受控制的变异，甚至自发燃烧等现象。这就是为什么我们会携带催化剂的原因——经过处理的神秘水晶显然更容易成为野性魔法释放的目标；相信我，你总宁愿自己手中的昂贵法杖碎裂，也不愿自己的大脑从鼻子里流出来吧。 然而，只要运用得当，魔法通常都是相当可预测的。当你施展某个法术时火球术每次你施放这个法术时，都会有一团火焰从你的手掌中射出，然后沿着你指定的方向飞去，在到达目标点时爆炸。这团火焰的飞行轨迹就像一支射出的箭一样呈弧线形态，影响范围大约有二十英尺。不过，你并不总能得到想要的结果——仅仅因为你进行了这样的尝试而已。火球术对某人使用这个法术并不意味着你会攻击他们——只要你正确地施放这个法术，它就会产生可靠且可重复的效果。 如今，埃斯特洛尔学院将其所有的法术分类为四大类，这些分类是根据这些法术之间的共同特性来进行的。每个类别或学派都有一批专门研究该领域的学者们，他们不断深入探索其中的奥秘，创造新的法术，以此提升自己所在学派在学院中的地位。这些研究竞争异常激烈，然而，往往都是咒术学派最终取得胜利——至少是因为他们在这个领域拥有垄断地位。火球术。
rows.raw: " The first recorded practitioners of what we would call magic were tribal shamans, who passed their little-understood hedgecraft down through a well developed oral tradition. With each successive generation, the chaotic magics of these shamans was explored ever more deeply, slowly refined through trial and error and experimentation across uncounted centuries. I can only imagine how many shamans were lost to wild, consumptive magic escaping their control as they fumbled in the dark for a greater understanding of that deadly ancestral arts. When the great dragons of Aerimarne taught their dragonclaw script to the early Belharans, it is said that High King Ramius's first command was that his shamans and oracles use the new script to impress the syllables that made up their words of power into clay, so that their knowledge could be distributed across his kingdom. Thus, the first spellbooks were created — or spell tablets, more accurately, but the point stands: from then on, magic became standardized, the knowledge spread in a web of magical mastery across the early empire. Soon, any scholar capable of reading the dragonmarks was allowed to learn spellcraft, rather than an art only taught between shamanic master and apprentices. My contemporaries in the grand academy of Estelore attribute this royal decree with beginning Belhar's rise to power, and there is likely some grain of truth to that belief; certainly, Belhar has the largest and most well-developed cadre of magisters the world has ever seen at its command, from the Spellblades of Maidenbridge to the Mage-Priests of Nareva to the Arch-magisters of Estelore. The patronage of Belhar's emperors has allowed magic to evolve from hedgecraft and superstition to a topic of research as accessible as history or economics. Even the distant priest-kings of Kitsuhon cannot match the empire for its peerless mastery of the arcane. But, my dear reader, what is it that these vaunted magisters study today? The college of Estelore defines a spell, the archetypal example of magic used in the world, thusly: "Any conscious, controlled invocation of aetheric energy channeled into a repeatable, predictable shape." Spellcraft is at the heart of anyone's understanding of magic, as it is how we interact with magic. To craft a spell, a would-be magister needs three things: the first is knowledge. Spells are memorized, ritual invocations that make use of specific words of power, ancient draconic syllables chanted in specific orders that prime the ambient aetheric energy around the caster. These words must be spoken forcefully and clearly, as a single misspoken phrase can change the nature of the spell, twisting it out of the caster's control. This is why a catalyst of some kind is necessary to safely cast a spell: should a spell go wild and awry, it is possible to focus the backlash into a treated arcane object and away from the caster. Without a catalyst, the discharged wild magic will have nowhere to go but the caster. Lastly, a mage needs force of will. The aether is inherently entropic, and left to its own devices does nothing; through the words of power, a mage can shape magic to her will, but it requires a great force of will to discharge the spell. This execution is also commensurately draining; more powerful spells require greater experience and will to cast, and sap more strength from the mage in the casting. I have more than once now mentioned wild magic. Perhaps it is time to address that most dangerous mammoth in the barn. A misspoken word of power, or a lack of sufficient will to execute a spell, can cause magic to slip out of the caster's control. Aetheric energy inherently wishes to be discharged — keeping a spell going for more than a momentary invocation demands a great deal of focused concentration, and artifacts that constantly channel magic are rare wonders indeed. Without a proper outlet (ie., a spell), the magical energy will discharge itself in what thus far scholars have conceded appears to be entirely random ways. The unfortunate caster often ends up acting as a lightning rod, attracting the power of the foiled spell back into herself, with predictably disastrous consequences — brain hemorrhage, uncontrolled mutation, or even spontaneous combustions are among the effects I have myself witnessed befall other mages. This is, again, why we carry catalysts, as a treated arcane crystal apparently acts as a more tempting target for wild magic to discharge into; and believe me, you would rather have an expensive wand shatter in your hand than have your brain liquify out of your nose. When controlled properly, however, magic is generally fairly predictable. When you invoke the spell Fireball, every time you cast the spell a ball of fire will lance out from your palm and detonate at a point you aimed at, arcing much like a loosed arrow, and washing over a radius of some twenty feet. You may not always get the results you want — just because you throw a Fireball at someone doesn't mean you'll hit them — but so long as you execute the spell correctly, it will produce reliable and repeatable effects. The college of Estelore today divides its catalog of spells into four broad categories, based on related properties. Each category, or school, has a devoted following of magisters who specialize in it, delving ever deeper into its mysteries and crafting new spells to further their specialty's prestige within the college. Their studies are downright competitive, though alas it is always the school of conjuration that is destined to win — if only because they have the monopoly on Fireballs. "

rows.original:
Conjuration magic excites elemental energies into being, allowing mages to call forth terrible flames or bathe their foes in acid. Most conjurations are instantaneous evocations of energy: a snap freeze or blast of fire.
        
        More advanced conjuration magic allows for the summoning of energy or even entire spirits from beyond the Ways: typically in the form of elementals which can be bound to serve their conjurer for the span of a few minutes. Maintaining a conjuration for more than a moment requires a substantial force of will and absolute concentration, lest the summoned energy — or worse, bound spirit — spiral wildly out of control. Once a conjurer ends a spell, any lingering energy quickly dissipates: creating anything lasting through magic is the domain of enchantment, and there are countless stories of conjurers forgetting this lesson to their (often terminal) detriment.
        
        As Estelore's understanding of interplanar travel and the Ways Between expands, it has been the Grand School of Conjuration that has taken the lead in researching this exciting new branch of magical lore. It is the Grand Magister's hope that some day soon, it will be possible through a mere spell to carve a portal between planes, or travel directly to the Ways. 
        
        In the fifteenth year of Her Holy Majesty the Empress Julianna Harasii's reign, Grand Magister Caedwynn var Clare represents the Grand School of Conjuration at the College of Estelore.
rows.translation:
咒术魔法能够将元素能量凝聚成形，使法师们能够召唤出可怕的火焰，或是让敌人陷入酸液的侵蚀之中。大多数咒术都是对能量的一种瞬间操控：无论是瞬间冰冻敌人，还是释放火球攻击。
        
        更高级的咒术魔法能够召唤来自彼岸的能量，甚至是完整的灵魂：这些被召唤的存在通常以元素生物的形式出现，它们可以被束缚起来，在几分钟的时间内为施法者服务。维持一个法术的效果超过片刻，需要强大的意志力与高度的专注力，否则被召唤出来的能量——或者更糟糕的是，被束缚的灵魂——就会失控地肆意蔓延。一旦施法者结束了法术，任何残留的能量都会迅速消散：要想通过魔法创造出持久存在的物体，那就必须依靠“附魔”这一技巧了。而关于施法者忘记这一道理，从而招致严重后果的故事更是数不胜数。
        
        随着埃斯托洛对星际旅行以及那些神秘通道的了解不断深入，大魔法学院成为了研究这一令人兴奋的新魔法领域的先锋。大法师们满怀期望，希望有朝一日，只需施展一个简单的咒语，就能在各个位面之间打开通道，或者直接前往那些神秘通道。 
        
        在朱莉安娜·哈拉西女皇统治的第十五个年头，大法师凯德温·瓦尔·克莱尔代表埃斯托洛尔学院的大魔法学系出席了会议。

rows.original: Enchantment is the art of binding magical energies into stable, usable forms for extended durations — and also the undoing of such artifice. The most common form of enchantment is the art of soulforging: taking the bound spirits of slain monsters and binding them into arms and armor. Soulbound artifacts take on some properties of the beast from which they are made, such as a sword that perpetually coats itself in lindwurm venom. There is no theoretical limit on how long an enchanted object can maintain its magic when properly treated with ley-crystal runes of binding, trapping the aetheric energy inside the item. Many magic weapons are generational heirlooms, passed down through noble houses or warrior orders. No doubt the most famous example of such a blade is the greatsword Maidenscythe, a weapon that fell from the sky like a meteor during the fiftieth year of Holy Emperor Claudio's reign and embedded itself in the wyld tree of Maidenbridge. The city's lords of House Errion took up the silvery sword, and over the years since it has accumulated countless spirits of the slain within its blade. Enchantment also covers the art of unbinding magic. Breaking the hold of a spell on another person or erecting protective wards against an enemy wizard are both uses of enchantment magic — the rare instantaneous use of the school. In the fifteenth year of Her Holy Majesty the Empress Julianna Harasii's reign, Arch-Magister Robrandt Blaque represents the Grand School of Enchantment at the College of Estelore.
rows.translation: 魔法附魔是将魔力转化为稳定、可使用的形态，并使其持续发挥效力的技艺——同时也包括解除这种人工创造的魔法效果。最常见的附魔形式就是“灵魂锻造”：将被消灭的怪物所蕴含的魔力提取出来，然后将其融入武器或盔甲之中。 被赋予魔力的物品在经过适当的处理后，能够持续保持其魔力。这种处理通常会使用束缚法术的秘纹，将这些以太能量封印在物品内部。因此，从理论上来说，这样的物品保持魔力的时间并没有限制。许多魔法武器都是世代相传的传家之宝，由贵族家族或战士组织代代相传。毫无疑问，这类武器的最著名代表就是那把巨剑。梅登西斯这把武器在神圣皇帝克劳迪乌斯统治的第五十年间，如同流星般从天而降，深深嵌入了梅登布里奇的野树之中。埃里恩家族的领主们掌握了这把银色宝剑，从那以后，它的剑刃里逐渐积聚了无数被斩杀之人的灵魂。 魔法也涵盖了解除魔法束缚的艺术。解除某人身上咒语的束缚，或是为抵御敌方巫师而设置防护结界，这些都属于魔法的应用范畴——这也是这种魔法体系极为罕见但确实存在的使用方式。 在朱莉安娜·哈拉西女皇统治的第十五个年头，大法师罗布兰特·布莱克代表埃斯托洛尔学院中的魔法大学出席了相关会议。

rows.original:
In its most widely-used form, transmutation magic is used across the world by priests and hedge witches to mend cuts and scrapes, sooth burns and bruises, and accelerate the healing of cleanly broken bones. Healing magic cannot restore lost limbs or cure virulent diseases, but minor injuries and most poisons can be alleviated through simple spells. 
        
        Transmutation magic is also used by mage-smiths to quickly and efficiently shape metals into useful tools and weapons. With more training, such spells can be used to alter the alchemical properties of a substance, making it lighter or heavier or reimagining its shape without the heat of the forge. 
        
        In its most advanced form, transmutation can even reshape living creatures' bodies by the same principal as it can be used to heal wounds. This particular use of transmutation magic is widely considered the most difficult and dangerous form of magic to master, as even slight lapses in concentration while casting can twist the caster (or unfortunate subject) into a malformed abomination. 
        
        In the fifteenth year of Her Holy Majesty the Empress Julianna Harasii's reign, Arch-Magister Viona var Este represents the Grand School of Transmutation at the College of Estelore.
-
rows.translation:
在最为常见的应用形式中，变形魔法被世界各地的牧师和草药师们用来治疗割伤、擦伤，缓解烧伤和淤青，以及加速干净断裂的骨骼的愈合过程。治疗魔法无法让失去的肢体重新生长，也无法治愈致命的疾病，但通过一些简单的法术，它确实能够缓解轻伤以及大多数中毒症状。 
        
        炼金术士们也利用转化魔法来快速而高效地将金属加工成实用的工具和武器。通过更多的练习，这类法术甚至可以改变物质的炼金属性，使其变得更轻或更重，或者在不需高温锻造的情况下改变其形状。 
        
        在最为高级的形态下，转化魔法甚至能够利用同样的原理重塑生物的躯体，同时也能用于治愈伤口。这种特定形式的转化魔法被广泛认为是最难掌握、也最危险的魔法类型，因为在施法过程中哪怕稍有分心，都可能导致施法者或目标生物变成形态畸变的怪物。 
        
        在朱莉安娜·哈拉西女皇统治的第十五个年头，大法师维奥娜·瓦尔·埃斯特代表埃斯特洛尔学院中的转化大学派出席了会议。

rows.original:
Illusion magic creatures unreal sensory effects, or alters the perception of other creatures. Common illusions allow for mages to change how they look to others, adopting different clothes or physical shapes, or create fantastical sensory tricks like showers of sparks and roiling fogs. More advanced illusionists can create duplicates of themselves, or cause their foes to believe themselves surrounded by flames or that the ground is swallowing them up. 

        Some illusionists even learn to twist a creature's thoughts around, confusing their allegiances or even implanting unbidden desires and guilts. It is possible to implant entire phantasmal worlds that consume the mind, trapping the poor victim in a world of the illusionist's creation. Other spells can modify or remove memories, or even change the victim's personality. Needless to say, this particular use of magic is considered taboo throughout the civilized world, and the college takes a dim view on mages that abuse these powers for their own amusement.
        
        In the fifteenth year of Her Holy Majesty the Empress Julianna Harasii's reign, Arch-Magister Sigismund the Blind represents the Grand School of Illusion at the College of Estelore.
rows.translation:
幻术魔法生物能够产生虚幻的感官效果，或者改变其他生物的感知方式。常见的幻术能够让法师改变自己在他人眼中的形象——比如更换服装或改变外形，或者制造出火花飞溅、迷雾缭绕等奇幻的感官效果。更高级的幻术师能够制造出自己的分身，或者让敌人误以为自己被火焰包围，或者觉得地面正在将他们吞噬。

        有些幻术师甚至能够操控生物的思维，混淆他们的忠诚立场，甚至在他们心中植入不必要的欲望与负罪感。完全有可能创造出那些能够吞噬人类思维的虚幻世界，将可怜的受害者困在幻术师创造出来的幻想之中。其他一些法术则可以修改或抹去记忆，甚至改变受害者的性格。毋庸置疑，这种特殊的魔法运用在整个文明世界都被视为禁忌，而学院也对那些为了取乐而滥用这些力量的法师们持负面态度。
        
        在朱莉安娜·哈拉西女皇统治的第十五年，盲人大法师西吉斯蒙德代表幻术大学参加了埃斯托洛尔学院的会议。
rows.raw:
"
        Illusion magic creatures unreal sensory effects, or alters the perception of other creatures. Common illusions allow for mages to change how they look to others, adopting different clothes or physical shapes, or create fantastical sensory tricks like showers of sparks and roiling fogs. More advanced illusionists can create duplicates of themselves, or cause their foes to believe themselves surrounded by flames or that the ground is swallowing them up. 

        Some illusionists even learn to twist a creature's thoughts around, confusing their allegiances or even implanting unbidden desires and guilts. It is possible to implant entire phantasmal worlds that consume the mind, trapping the poor victim in a world of the illusionist's creation. Other spells can modify or remove memories, or even change the victim's personality. Needless to say, this particular use of magic is considered taboo throughout the civilized world, and the college takes a dim view on mages that abuse these powers for their own amusement.
        
        In the fifteenth year of Her Holy Majesty the Empress Julianna Harasii's reign, Arch-Magister Sigismund the Blind represents the Grand School of Illusion at the College of Estelore.
        "

rows.original: —Lady Kalypso of Tychris Belhar survived the Godswar — barely. Its society and unity were shattered, divided under the rule of disparate potentates and city-states. Its economy was wrecked, capable of little production let alone long-distance trade. Many of the people who had worked on the land were dead, leaving agricultural production at terrifyingly low levels. Those that remained had their hands full feeding themselves, let alone producing enough food to allow others to live in cities (or, indeed, military camps) without farming their own food. These were the things that ended the era of the great lockstep legions, not stupidity or obscurantism. The people who lived in the Empire did not forget how to make complex war on a large scale; they simply lacked the resources to do so. Individual cities or warlords could not muster the vast professional armies that the united imperials had been able to, and given their losses, even if the Empire had still been united, the imperials would not have been able to do so, either. What was left was societies that only contained very small groups of people that had the resources to maintain the ability to fight, let alone spend all of their time on it in ways sufficient to become good at it. Only the wealthiest of elites could finance training, armor, and good weapons. This meant that those whom historians often call 'the powerful'[silly| — but not in a Byzantine sense; this is not the place for following the debate over the dynatoi but please know that the author of this Codex entry does not take the old Ostrogorsky thesis of them being an outright Western-style aristocracy seriously —] were the ones who did most of the fighting. In this they would usually be accompanied by small groups of trained and experienced retainers, albeit usually of lesser military quality; only very rarely would larger groups of people leave their land, flocks, fish, or towns to take up arms as untrained levies. Sometimes the 'powerful' fought for a particular ruler or city; other times, they would turn mercenary, crossing boundaries to battle for whomever they pleased if price and land were right. Whether they inherited it from aristocratic Belharan parents or took it by force in battle, they were the ones who controlled most of what little wealth existed in the lean years following the apocalypse, and thus most of the modern noble houses count them as ancestors. Ironically, the slowly growing prosperity of the last century has upset this state of affairs. Now, many realms and city-states have the resources and population to build larger armies... and, less happily, there's enough food in most parts of the world to sustain larger groups of bandits preying on farmers, shepherds, and fishers. City-states field forces of citizen militia who arm themselves out of their personal wealth; princes and princesses can call on their "friends", warriors of note with their own groups of retainers. Mighty Khor'minos has even gone a long way toward recreating Old Belhar's lockstep legions, as has Taelia on a somewhat smaller scale. And with more food and wealth in abundance, mercenary companies have emerged, especially in the Heartlands and Tronarii. Mercenaries in particular bear mention as a fungible quantity. A mercenary company (and they are almost always organized in companies; a single warrior without a support network of some kind is essentially useless and usually dead) can move from war to war in the Heartlands more or less seamlessly, provided its leaders, who are usually aristocracy or of the untitled wealthy, survive as a nucleus around which to recruit fresh warriors. But while they may seem common now compared to several years ago, there are still not all that many compared to the days of yore. Growing prosperity is one thing, but it will be many decades, if not centuries, before there is enough food to feed large groups of warriors who do not cultivate their own crops. As a result, even the largest mercenary companies tend to keep barely a hundred or so spears in their establishment. More than that they cannot pay. Well do the Heartlanders remember the tragedies that resulted when the Khushkan entrepreneurs hired on more warriors than they could pay or feed — a whirlwind march of conquest in a desperate effort to keep their forces together, and then, when they faced defeat, a turn to dark powers that nearly turned tragedy into apocalypse. As ever, the best-trained and -equipped warriors remain the small groups of paladins and champions that comprise the military orders of the Seven. (In fact, the very word paladin exists because the greatest founding members of the divine military orders came from the Belharan palace bodyguards, or palatini. The Lumian Warriors of White trace their lineage directly to the imperial Candidati, an elite formation of palatine soldiers set apart because they wore white robes with their armor.) After the Godswar, many temporal leaders quibbled about these divine warriors, who for the most part remained outside their direct control. But despite some friction, no one seriously considered eliminating the organizations that had saved civilization, and both nobles and ordinary people continued to donate to the gods and sacrifice to them, supplying the resources that enabled the military orders to continue to do their work. The Astrida continued to keep dangerous portals closed, the valkyries continued to fight their long twilight war against the remnants of the Wraith-touched, the Tiran paladins continued to destroy undead, and so on. Thanks to this, all of them, both godsworn and more mortal paladins, have more experience and more training than almost any other warriors in the known world.
rows.translation: ——提克里斯的卡吕普索女士 贝哈尔在神战之中幸存了下来——但仅仅是幸存而已。它的社会结构与团结早已瓦解，分裂成了由各个势力与城邦统治的碎片。它的经济也遭到了毁灭，几乎无法进行任何生产，更遑论开展长途贸易了。许多曾在土地上劳作的人已经去世，导致农业生产水平降到了极其低的程度。那些幸存下来的人也忙于养活自己，更无暇生产足够的食物，让其他人能够在城市里（或者军营里）生活而不需要自己耕种食物。正是这些因素终结了那些规模庞大、行动高度统一的军团时代，而非愚蠢或愚昧。生活在帝国内的人们并没有忘记如何进行大规模的复杂战争；他们只是缺乏进行这种战争所需的资源罢了。单个城市或军阀们根本无法组建出像统一后的帝国那样庞大的专业军队。考虑到他们所遭受的损失，即使帝国依然保持统一，那些地方势力也同样无法做到这一点。 最终剩下的，只有那些拥有足够资源来维持自身战斗能力、更不用说进行其他消耗的社会了。所有在他们所处的时代，只有那些能够承担训练费用、购买精良盔甲与武器的人，才有可能真正掌握这些技能。因此，那些被历史学家称为“权贵”的人，恰恰是这类人。[silly| — 但并不是以那种复杂繁琐的方式；这里并不是讨论这些问题的合适场所。dynatoi但请注意，这份文献的作者并不认同奥斯特罗戈尔斯基关于他们属于纯粹西方式贵族阶层的观点。]正是这些人承担了大部分战斗任务。在执行这些任务时，他们通常会有一小群受过训练、经验丰富的随从陪同，不过这些随从的军事素质通常较低；只有极少数情况下，才会有更多的人离开他们的土地、牧场、渔场或城镇，以未经训练的平民身份拿起武器参战。有时候，这些“有权势”的人会为某位统治者或某座城市而战；而有时候，他们会选择成为雇佣兵，跨越边界，为那些愿意支付合适报酬并提供土地的人效力。无论他们是继承了贝尔哈兰贵族父母的财产，还是通过战斗夺取了权力，在大灾变后的那些艰难岁月里，正是他们掌控了几乎所有有限的财富。因此，现代的许多贵族家族都将他们视为自己的祖先。 具有讽刺意味的是，上个世纪逐渐发展的繁荣状况打破了这种平衡。如今，许多王国和城邦已经拥有了组建更庞大军队的资源和人口……而更不幸的是，世界上大多数地区都拥有足够的食物，足以养活那些劫掠农民、牧民和渔民的盗匪团伙。城邦们依靠公民自筹资金组建民兵部队；王子和公主们则可以召集他们的“朋友”——那些拥有自己私人扈从队伍的知名战士。强大的科尔米诺斯在重现古贝尔哈尔那种严整的军团编制方面取得了显著进展，而塔莉娅也在较小规模上进行了类似的尝试。随着食物和财富的日益丰富，雇佣兵组织应运而生，尤其是在中心地带和特洛纳里地区。 尤其是雇佣兵，他们可以被视作一种可替代的力量。一支雇佣兵队伍（这类队伍几乎总是以团队形式组织起来的；没有相应支援网络的单独战士基本上毫无用处，通常也会丧命）可以在中央地带的一场战争转移到另一场战争中，而且这种转移过程几乎可以顺利进行，前提是他们的领导者——这些领导者通常属于贵族阶层或那些没有正式头衔但却非常富有的阶层——能够存活下来，并继续作为核心来招募新的战士。不过，尽管如此看起来似乎与几年前相比，这种情况已经变得普遍了，但与过去相比，数量仍然不算多。经济的繁荣确实是一个积极因素，但要想让那些不从事农业生产的大型战士群体有足够的食物吃，恐怕还需要几十甚至几百年的时间。因此，即便是规模最大的雇佣兵公司，其手中也往往只保留着一百来支长矛而已。超过这个数量，他们就无力支付相关费用了。那些居住在腹地的人们，想必还记得当年库什坎的商人们因为雇佣了超过他们财力所能承担数量的战士，而引发的一系列悲剧——他们拼命试图维持军队的战斗力，因此展开了疯狂的征服行动；而当遭遇失败时，他们又求助于暗影势力，这些势力几乎将悲剧变成了毁灭性的灾难。 与往常一样，训练有素、装备精良的战士们，依然是由那些圣骑士和小英雄们组成的小队，他们构成了七大军事组织的中坚力量。（事实上，这个词本身……）圣骑士它的存在，正是因为那些神圣军事组织最初的创立者大多来自贝尔哈兰宫殿的护卫队。帕拉蒂尼白之卢米安战士们的血脉，可直接追溯到那位皇帝。候选人这是一支由宫廷士兵组成的精英部队，他们之所以被称为精英，是因为他们穿着白色长袍，同时也会穿戴盔甲。在神战之后，许多世俗领袖对这些神圣战士议论纷纷，因为这些战士在很大程度上并不受他们的直接控制。尽管存在一些矛盾和冲突，但没有人真正考虑过废除那些拯救了人类的组织。无论是贵族还是普通民众，都继续向这些神明捐赠财物、献上祭品，从而为这些军事组织提供所需的资源，使它们能够继续履行自己的职责。阿斯特里达继续关闭那些危险的传送门，女武神们继续进行着这场漫长的黄昏之战，对抗那些被怨灵影响的残余势力，蒂拉教会的圣骑士们也继续消灭那些不死生物，等等。正因如此，无论是那些受神明庇佑的圣骑士，还是那些更为平凡的圣骑士们，他们都比已知世界中几乎所有的战士都拥有更多的经验与更丰富的训练经历。

rows.original: "Among warriors with no access to the proper ceremonies, the rituals for Sorra's blessing of storms in battle are these: first and most efficacious, chanting the lay of Heaven's Air; second, offering a willow wreath or a leananstone to a well, or to the sea; third, chasing dogs while asking the sky for rain; last, shouting angrily and throwing a javelin at the sky."
rows.translation: 对于那些无法举行正规仪式的战士们来说，在战斗中祈求索拉赐予风暴的仪式如下：首先，也是最有效的方法，就是吟诵《天风之歌》；其次，可以将柳枝花环或利奈安石献给水井或大海；第三，可以在驱赶狗群的同时向天空祈求降雨；最后，就是愤怒地呼喊着将标枪投向天空。

rows.original: —Enno, Taelian priest of Sorra Old Belhar's lockstep legions marched around the world winning victory after victory under monarchs and generals like Sanna Rutiliana, Edivus II, and Michael Melissenos, but Belharan aristocratic society also valorized leisure; a noble who had profited enough to allow himself or herself to avoid having to work had time for politics or the opportunity to dabble in civic, magical, or scientific pursuits, after all. In this era, though, warriors are at the top of the social hierarchy in nearly every culture that exists amid the wreckage of the empire, and it's not merely because of their wealth and power. Heartlander aristocrats have their position because of their military bona fides earned by protecting the city or the realm from foreign threats. So do the untitled wealthy whom the city-states of the south elect as generals over their citizen militia. For their part, tribal warriors like those of the Sailgraves orcs are the ones who bring plunder and slaves from the mainland back to their windswept isles, making a difference between subsistence and a semblance of prosperity... at least for those selfsame warriors. Being a warrior is key to the identity of the 'powerful' in much of the post-imperial world. Perhaps only in Khor'minos and some of the great independent cities like Barania and Marouka is there a semblance of the old Belharan sense of noble leisure used for the benefit of everyone else. Those warrior-aristocrats and champions who possess literary or musical ability usually write about their way of life, and those with money pay for the same from the troubadours and bards of Savarra's byways. Elite culture, however, is not the only place for tales of war and songs of battle. The poor hear them (and sing them) as well. To be sure, a peasant's viewpoint often (fairly) depicts warriors as the rapacious thugs who enslave children, ravish families, steal crops and livestock, or just casually murder people. But some figures of song like Goar, a tragic hero of the Khushkan war, have more positive depictions among ordinary Savarrans. And, of course, Lumia's valkyries, Nareva's Astrida, and paladins of every deity are almost universally admired in both aristocratic and peasant culture for both military prowess and saving the innocent regardless of wealth or station. These stories and songs circulate as more or less common currency throughout the lands that once lived under imperial rule. From Tronarii to Tychris, it is reasonable to say that the post-imperial peoples all have shared expectations of what warfare is like. Warriors bound together not just by a common tongue and common religion (even if one god or another of the Seven happens to predominate in a given land) but by common experiences (especially for mercenary companies, which can operate in lands very far afield) tend to have similar views about what is acceptable in war. This does not mean that battle is the same for the mountaineers of Zhenna as it is for the urban militia of Taelia or the woodsmen and wyld elves of Sartanni, but it can mean that all of those groups would have similar understandings of what constitutes an acceptable target in the eyes of their peoples and their gods. All of the Seven are, in some form or another, deities of war. Generals might pray to Nareva or Keros when employing clever stratagems, to Mallach for soldierly unity and comradeship, to Sorra for favorable weather, or to Velun when seeking a wild battle frenzy. Lumia, of course, is the patron goddess of just war: defending against attackers, or bringing fire and sword down upon the truly wicked. But Tira perhaps embodies the spirit of warriors best, for she is not merely the goddess of battle and death but the goddess of chance and fate. Everyone who bears arms in Savarra knows that war is the province of uncertainty, that the results of most battles amount to a roll of the dice (or, by common metaphor, Tira's bones). In such circumstances, who better to have on one's side than the goddess who decrees mortals' allotted time?
rows.translation: —恩诺，索拉的女祭司塔埃利安 在桑娜·鲁蒂利安娜、埃迪瓦斯二世和米迦尔·梅利塞诺斯等君主与将军的领导下，老贝哈尔那纪律严明的军团横扫天下，屡获胜利，然而贝哈尔的贵族社会此外那些拥有充裕闲暇时间的贵族们，由于财富充足，无需劳作，因此有时间从事政治活动，或者有机会涉足公民事务、魔法研究或科学探索。然而，在这个时代，几乎在帝国残余势力所影响的每一个文化中，战士们都处于社会阶层的顶端——而这并不仅仅是因为他们的财富和权力。腹地的贵族们之所以能够获得这样的地位，是因为他们通过保护城市或王国免受外来威胁而赢得了军事上的声誉。那些没有头衔但却拥有财富的人也是如此——他们被南方的一些城邦选为将军，来领导这些城邦的民兵组织。对于那些部落战士来说，就像帆葬群岛兽人这样的战士们，正是他们将大陆上的战利品和奴隶带回那些被狂风肆虐的岛屿，才使得这些岛屿上的居民得以维持生计，甚至过上相对繁荣的生活。至少对那些战士来说是这样。成为一名战士在后帝国时代的许多地区，这种观念正是“权贵”身份认同的关键所在。或许只有在科尔米诺斯，以及巴拉尼亚和马鲁卡这样一些伟大的独立城市中，才还保留着那种古老的贝拉兰式的贵族休闲观念——那种旨在造福所有人的休闲方式。 那些兼具文学或音乐才能的武士贵族与英雄们，通常会将自己的生活方式记录下来；而那些财力雄厚的人，则会出资让萨瓦拉乡间的游吟诗人和吟游者来创作这类作品。然而，精英文化并非讲述战争故事、吟唱战斗之歌的唯一场所。穷人也能够听到这些歌声。事实上，从农民的角度来看，战士们往往被描绘成那些贪婪的暴徒——他们奴役儿童，毁坏家庭，抢走农作物和牲畜，甚至随意杀人。然而，像库什坎战争中的悲剧英雄戈阿尔这样的歌中人物，在普通的萨瓦兰人中却得到了更为积极的评价。当然，卢米娅的英灵们、娜瑞瓦的阿斯特里达，以及每一位神明所派遣的圣骑士们，无论是在贵族文化还是农民阶层中，都因其卓越的军事才能以及无论贫富、地位高低都致力于拯救无辜者的行为而受到普遍的钦佩。 这些故事和歌曲在曾经处于帝国统治之下的那些地区，以或多或少的普遍性被人们传颂着。从特洛纳里到提克里斯，可以说，后帝国时代的各个民族对于战争的认知都是相似的。那些不仅因为使用相同的语言、信奉相同的宗教（即使在某个特定地区，七大神明中的某一位可能更为人们所尊崇），而且因为共同经历过一些事情而团结在一起的战士们——尤其是那些能够在遥远地区活动的雇佣军组织——往往会对战争中什么是可以接受的持有相似的看法。这并不意味着，对于珍娜的山地居民来说，战斗的方式与泰利亚的城市民兵或萨塔尼的森林居民与野精灵们是相同的，但可以肯定的是，这些群体对于什么才算是他们族群及其神明所认可的可攻击目标，都有着大致相同的理解。 这七神，无论以何种形式存在，都属于战争之神。将领们在运用巧妙的战略时，可能会向娜瑞瓦或凯罗斯祈祷；在寻求士兵们的团结与友谊时，会向马拉赫祈求；在希望天气对作战有利时，会向索拉祈祷；而当他们渴望引发一场激烈的野战时，则会向维伦祈求。当然，卢米娅正是正义之战的女神：她守护人们免受攻击者的侵害，也会用火与剑惩罚那些真正的恶人。但或许蒂拉最能体现战士的精神，因为她不仅是战斗与死亡的女神，更是机遇与命运的女神。在萨瓦拉，每一个持械作战的人都知道，战争充满了不确定性，大多数战役的结果其实就如同掷骰子一样充满随机性（或者用人们常说的比喻来说，就是取决于提拉的神谕）。在这种情况下，还有谁比那位决定凡人生命时限的女神更值得我们信赖呢？
rows.raw: "—Enno, Taelian priest of Sorra Old Belhar's lockstep legions marched around the world winning victory after victory under monarchs and generals like Sanna Rutiliana, Edivus II, and Michael Melissenos, but Belharan aristocratic society also valorized leisure; a noble who had profited enough to allow himself or herself to avoid having to work had time for politics or the opportunity to dabble in civic, magical, or scientific pursuits, after all. In this era, though, warriors are at the top of the social hierarchy in nearly every culture that exists amid the wreckage of the empire, and it's not merely because of their wealth and power. Heartlander aristocrats have their position because of their military bona fides earned by protecting the city or the realm from foreign threats. So do the untitled wealthy whom the city-states of the south elect as generals over their citizen militia. For their part, tribal warriors like those of the Sailgraves orcs are the ones who bring plunder and slaves from the mainland back to their windswept isles, making a difference between subsistence and a semblance of prosperity... at least for those selfsame warriors. Being a warrior is key to the identity of the 'powerful' in much of the post-imperial world. Perhaps only in Khor'minos and some of the great independent cities like Barania and Marouka is there a semblance of the old Belharan sense of noble leisure used for the benefit of everyone else. Those warrior-aristocrats and champions who possess literary or musical ability usually write about their way of life, and those with money pay for the same from the troubadours and bards of Savarra's byways. Elite culture, however, is not the only place for tales of war and songs of battle. The poor hear them (and sing them) as well. To be sure, a peasant's viewpoint often (fairly) depicts warriors as the rapacious thugs who enslave children, ravish families, steal crops and livestock, or just casually murder people. But some figures of song like Goar, a tragic hero of the Khushkan war, have more positive depictions among ordinary Savarrans. And, of course, Lumia's valkyries, Nareva's Astrida, and paladins of every deity are almost universally admired in both aristocratic and peasant culture for both military prowess and saving the innocent regardless of wealth or station. These stories and songs circulate as more or less common currency throughout the lands that once lived under imperial rule. From Tronarii to Tychris, it is reasonable to say that the post-imperial peoples all have shared expectations of what warfare is like. Warriors bound together not just by a common tongue and common religion (even if one god or another of the Seven happens to predominate in a given land) but by common experiences (especially for mercenary companies, which can operate in lands very far afield) tend to have similar views about what is acceptable in war. This does not mean that battle is the same for the mountaineers of Zhenna as it is for the urban militia of Taelia or the woodsmen and wyld elves of Sartanni, but it can mean that all of those groups would have similar understandings of what constitutes an acceptable target in the eyes of their peoples and their gods. All of the Seven are, in some form or another, deities of war. Generals might pray to Nareva or Keros when employing clever stratagems, to Mallach for soldierly unity and comradeship, to Sorra for favorable weather, or to Velun when seeking a wild battle frenzy. Lumia, of course, is the patron goddess of just war: defending against attackers, or bringing fire and sword down upon the truly wicked. But Tira perhaps embodies the spirit of warriors best, for she is not merely the goddess of battle and death but the goddess of chance and fate. Everyone who bears arms in Savarra knows that war is the province of uncertainty, that the results of most battles amount to a roll of the dice (or, by common metaphor, Tira's bones). In such circumstances, who better to have on one's side than the goddess who decrees mortals' allotted time? "

rows.original: "Audacious? Certainly. Reckless? Perhaps. But I say to you now, to be more cautious would embrace certain defeat. Take refuge in our audacity. They expect us to demonstrate in front of our camp, not attack."
rows.translation: 大胆？当然。鲁莽？也许吧。但我现在要告诉你们，过于谨慎反而会招致失败。让我们依靠自己的大胆吧。他们期望我们在营地前展示实力，而不是发动攻击。
rows.raw: '\n        "Audacious? Certainly. Reckless? Perhaps. But I say to you now, to be more cautious would embrace certain defeat. Take refuge in our audacity. They expect us to demonstrate in front of our camp, not attack."\n        '

rows.original: —Michael Melissenos, Belharan general, shortly before the Battle of Satricum In every society around the world, warriors fight in different ways, and those ways are dependent on the society that produces them and the arms and armor available to them.[silly| Sometimes silly stuff still seeps through, like gigantic broadswords for defeating plate armor that doesn't exist, or war hammers for a similar purpose, but inevitably in games like these, aesthetics trump strict lore accuracy. Don't worry about them.] Weapons and protection are the tools of the trade, and tactics the method. Bronze weapons and gear remain the favored choice of all those who can afford them, but thanks to the labor (and rare tin ore) that goes into making military-worthy bronze, they are uncommon outside the warrior elite. In fact, their price forces even aristocrats into economies. When wearing body armor, many warriors concentrate their bronze around their vitals and cover much of the rest with thick textiles, such as laminated linen or layered wool. Similarly, the trusty bronze spear is usually the weapon of choice, not least because it requires less bronze than does a larger war-axe or sword; it may be complemented by a bronze dagger or hand axe as a sidearm. Anyone who uses more bronze than that is truly a wealthy individual. Many cannot even muster that much bronze, and are forced to use weapons of relatively soft iron, sharpened wood, or stone. Infantry remains the core of most fighting forces, with obvious exceptions like pastoral herding tribes (who favor horseback) or centaurs (who must rely on allies or subjects if they want to field infantry). Usually, the most experienced warriors will be those who have the training to accurately employ ranged weapons like javelins, arrows, and especially magic, although a few veteran champions choose instead to make themselves well-armed and -armored enough to anchor a battle line often composed primarily of those less well-equipped. Combat generally begins with an exchange of missiles and, if applicable, magic, followed eventually by a clash of battle lines when the missiles are exhausted or when one side or the other can no longer stand the onslaught of arrows, javelins, and sling bullets. Centuries ago, Belharan notables preferred chariotry to slogging around on foot; chariots allowed great warriors to ride into battle quickly, or to stay mobile as they flung javelins or loosed arrows at the foe. Contact with centaur tribes and the gradual submission of the great herds changed this, as did the breeding of horses both large and small to carry single riders. Nowadays, despite Belhar's fall, chariots remain popular as ceremonial vehicles and in combat on relatively flat lands, but cavalry and centaury are becoming more and more prevalent for military purposes. Horse-riding bipeds and centaurs, usually in the same tribes, now dominate the great steppelands, herding stock and clashing over pasturage. It is these tribes that have begun to trade cavalry horses and camels as far afield as Tronarii, Yvennes, Gaba, and Jassira, all of which have begun to mount warriors of their own on them. Bipeds who ride horses often arm themselves with bows, javelins, or light spears to harass slower-moving infantry. Centaurs, however, remain the most prized hoof-warriors for would-be potentates, and the few taurs that deign to serve outside their tribe or herd often achieve positions of great military prominence. There are even small populations of other taur groups in the Heartlands, descendants of immigrants from long-lost lands once ruled by Old Belhar. Some are humpbacked and well-adapted to waterless places, others ferocious and strong with the fur and tails of lionesses. Battlemages are prized additions to any military force because of how few people (let alone warriors) have special magical education beyond a few casual cantrips — and because magic can have an outsize effect on any battlefield. The most favored large formation for infantry packs them together in large, fairly-dense blocks to keep soldiers from running away, but a well-placed concussive blast or chain lightning spell can tear the heart out of any such battle line. Since many infantry formations are effectively useless if they need to disperse, this means that in order for their own foot soldiers to stay together, battlemages spend as much of their time warding magic away from their own allies as they do casting offensive magic against the enemy. Because of this disproportionate effect in combat and their necessary separation from the rank and file — one cannot see where to cast spells if one is packed into the ranks with everyone else — battlemages often rise to command mercenary companies or achieve high rank in formal militaries. The fact that many of the military orders of the Seven are primarily composed of magic-wielding warriors (even if magic is not necessarily their strongest suit) is one of the things that makes them so impressive on the battlefield. Difficulties of command and control inhibit easy maneuver on the battlefield. Flank attacks, ambushes, feigned retreats, and the like are sometimes employed by large armies at the beginning of a fight according to a pre-agreed plan, especially if they contain well-trained troops, but complex evolutions in the midst of battle are usually beyond the abilities of large armies. In smaller groups — for example, warbands[silly| of between seven and thirty-five warriors, just as Ine intended] — shouted voices make complex orders and tactics much more viable. For larger armies, once fighting is joined, there is often little for a commander to do but hope their army is victorious; they cannot command beyond shouting range of their own voice, and they can rarely disengage their forces from a melee once committed. Often, then, the best thing for a commander to do is simply plunge into the fighting themselves, or to place themselves with one of the few groups that can take new orders mid-fighting: cavalry, chariotry, missile infantry, battlemages, or flying forces like valkyries and harpies.
rows.translation: —迈克尔·梅利塞诺斯，贝尔哈兰将军，在萨特里库姆战役前夕 在世界各地的每一个社会中，战士们的战斗方式各不相同，而这些战斗方式取决于他们所处的社会环境以及他们所拥有的武器和盔甲。[silly| 有时候，一些奇怪的设计还是会出现在游戏中，比如那些用来攻击板甲的巨型阔剑，其实这种武器根本不存在；又或者那些用于相同用途的战锤。但在这类游戏中，美观往往比严格的剧情设定更为重要。别太在意这些细节吧。]武器与护具是从事这一职业所必需的工具，而战术则是实现目标的方法。 对于那些有能力购买的人来说，青铜制武器与装备依然是他们的首选。然而，由于制造能够用于军事的青铜需要投入大量的劳动力以及稀有的锡矿资源，因此这类武器在战士精英之外极为罕见。事实上，它们的价格甚至迫使贵族也参与到这些经济活动中来。当穿戴护甲时，许多战士会将青铜材质主要集中在关键部位，而其余部位则用厚实的织物来覆盖，比如层压亚麻布或多层羊毛衣物。同样，可靠的青铜长矛通常是人们的首选武器，因为制造它所需的青铜量要比制作大型战斧或剑要少；人们还可以搭配使用青铜短匕或手斧作为副武器。而那些在武器制造上耗费更多青铜资源的人，无疑属于非常富有的阶层。许多人甚至连那么少量的青铜都凑不起，因此不得不使用由软铁制成的武器、经过打磨的木头或石头作为武器使用。 步兵仍然是大多数作战力量的核心，当然也有一些明显的例外，比如那些以放牧为生的部落（他们更倾向于使用骑兵），或者半人马族群（如果他们想要部署步兵，就必须依靠盟友或臣民的支持）。通常来说，经验最丰富的战士都是那些接受过训练、能够熟练使用投枪、箭矢这类远程武器的人，尤其是那些掌握魔法的人；不过也有一些资深战士选择让自己配备精良的武器和厚实的盔甲，从而成为主要由装备较差的士兵组成的战线的核心力量。战斗通常以双方交换导弹开始，如果适用的话，还会使用魔法。当导弹耗尽，或者其中一方再也无法承受箭矢、标枪和投石器的攻击时，战斗就会进入正面交锋阶段。 几个世纪前，贝拉兰的贵族们更喜欢乘坐战车而非步行作战；战车能够让勇猛的战士们迅速投入战斗，或者在投掷标枪或射箭攻击敌人时保持机动性。然而，与半人马部落的接触以及大型马群逐渐被驯化、小型马也被培育出来以供单人骑乘，这些因素都改变了这一状况。如今，尽管贝尔哈尔已经覆灭，但战车仍然在仪式场合以及相对平坦的地区被用作作战工具，而骑兵与半人马在军事领域中的使用也越来越普遍。这些骑马的生物以及半人马，通常属于同一个部落，如今已经掌控了那些广阔的草原，他们负责放牧牲畜，并为争夺牧场而发生冲突。正是这些部落开始将骑兵用的马匹和骆驼贩卖到遥远的特洛纳里、伊文尼斯、加巴和贾西拉等地，而这些地方也纷纷开始让自己的战士使用这些马匹进行作战。那些骑马作战的步兵通常会携带弓箭、标枪或轻矛，用来骚扰行动较慢的步兵部队。然而，半人马仍然是那些渴望成为强者的统治者们最为青睐的战斗力量。而那些愿意离开自己的部落或群体去为他人效力的半人马，往往能够获得举足轻重的军事地位。在中心地带，甚至还存在其他一些半人马族群，他们是那些来自遥远之地、曾经被古老的贝尔哈尔统治过的移民的后裔。有些体型驼背，且非常适应缺水环境；而另一些则凶猛强悍，它们的毛皮和尾巴酷似母狮的。 战斗法师是任何军事力量中极为宝贵的补充，因为很少有人（更不用说战士了）除了掌握一些简单的法术外，还接受过系统的魔法训练——而魔法在战场上往往能产生巨大的影响。对于步兵来说，最常用的密集作战编队就是将士兵们紧密地聚集在一起，这样就能防止他们逃跑。然而，一次位置恰到好处的震爆攻击或连锁闪电法术，就能彻底破坏这样的战斗阵型。由于许多步兵编队在需要分散行动时实际上会失去战斗力，因此为了使自己的步兵能够保持整齐队形，战斗法师们花费大量时间来阻挡针对自己盟友的魔法攻击，同时也花费同样多的时间来对敌人施展进攻性魔法。由于这种在战斗中产生的显著优势，以及他们必须与普通士兵区分开来——如果和其他人挤在一起，就根本无法确定在哪里施展法术——因此，战斗法师通常会担任雇佣军队伍的指挥官，或者在正规军队中取得高级职位。事实上，七人组发出的许多军事命令主要是由擅长使用魔法的战士组成的队伍（尽管魔法未必是他们最强大的武器），正是这种特点使得他们在战场上显得如此令人印象深刻。 然而，指挥与控制的难度却限制了他们在战场上的机动性。在战斗开始时，大型军队有时会根据事先约定的计划，采用侧翼进攻、埋伏、假意撤退等战术，尤其是当这些军队拥有训练有素的士兵时。然而，在战斗过程中进行复杂的战术调整，通常超出了大型军队的能力范围。在较小的团队中——比如那些游牧作战的部落。[silly| 由七名到三十五名战士组成，正如伊内所计划的那样。] — 喊叫声使复杂的指挥命令与战术策略得以有效实施。对于规模较大的军队而言，一旦战斗开始，指挥官往往无能为力，只能寄希望于自己的军队能够取得胜利；他们的指挥范围仅限于自己声音能够传达的范围之内，而且一旦军队陷入近战，也很难将部队撤出战斗状态。因此，对于指挥官来说，最明智的做法往往就是亲自投入战斗，或者加入那些能够在战斗中接受新命令的少数部队中：比如骑兵、战车部队、远程攻击步兵、战斗法师，以及像女武神和哈比这样的飞行部队。

Centuries ago, Belharan notables preferred chariotry to slogging around on foot; chariots allowed great warriors to ride into battle quickly, or to stay mobile as they flung javelins or loosed arrows at the foe. Contact with centaur tribes and the gradual submission of the great herds changed this, as did the breeding of horses both large and small to carry single riders. Nowadays, despite Belhar's fall, chariots remain popular as ceremonial vehicles and in combat on relatively flat lands, but cavalry and centaury are becoming more and more prevalent for military purposes. Horse-riding bipeds and centaurs, usually in the same tribes, now dominate the great steppelands, herding stock and clashing over pasturage. It is these tribes that have begun to trade cavalry horses and camels as far afield as Tronarii, Yvennes, Gaba, and Jassira, all of which have begun to mount warriors of their own on them. Bipeds who ride horses often arm themselves with bows, javelins, or light spears to harass slower-moving infantry. Centaurs, however, remain the most prized hoof-warriors for would-be potentates, and the few taurs that deign to serve outside their tribe or herd often achieve positions of great military prominence. There are even small populations of other taur groups in the Heartlands, descendants of immigrants from long-lost lands once ruled by Old Belhar. Some are humpbacked and well-adapted to waterless places, others ferocious and strong with the fur and tails of lionesses. Battlemages are prized additions to any military force because of how few people (let alone warriors) have special magical education beyond a few casual cantrips — and because magic can have an outsize effect on any battlefield. The most favored large formation for infantry packs them together in large, fairly-dense blocks to keep soldiers from running away, but a well-placed concussive blast or chain lightning spell can tear the heart out of any such battle line. Since many infantry formations are effectively useless if they need to disperse, this means that in order for their own foot soldiers to stay together, battlemages spend as much of their time warding magic away from their own allies as they do casting offensive magic against the enemy. Because of this disproportionate effect in combat and their necessary separation from the rank and file — one cannot see where to cast spells if one is packed into the ranks with everyone else — battlemages often rise to command mercenary companies or achieve high rank in formal militaries. The fact that many of the military orders of the Seven are primarily composed of magic-wielding warriors (even if magic is not necessarily their strongest suit) is one of the things that makes them so impressive on the battlefield. Difficulties of command and control inhibit easy maneuver on the battlefield. Flank attacks, ambushes, feigned retreats, and the like are sometimes employed by large armies at the beginning of a fight according to a pre-agreed plan, especially if they contain well-trained troops, but complex evolutions in the midst of battle are usually beyond the abilities of large armies. In smaller groups — for example, warbands[silly| of between seven and thirty-five warriors, just as Ine intended] — shouted voices make complex orders and tactics much more viable. For larger armies, once fighting is joined, there is often little for a commander to do but hope their army is victorious; they cannot command beyond shouting range of their own voice, and they can rarely disengage their forces from a melee once committed. Often, then, the best thing for a commander to do is simply plunge into the fighting themselves, or to place themselves with one of the few groups that can take new orders mid-fighting: cavalry, chariotry, missile infantry, battlemages, or flying forces like valkyries and harpies. "

rows.original: "You wicked children! How dare you? Sinning against your mothers and fathers, who conquered the world?"
rows.translation: 你们这些调皮的孩子！怎么敢这样？你们的行为是在背叛那些为你们征服世界的父母啊！

rows.original: —Antigone, general of the veteran Belharan Silver Shields, haranguing the opposing army shortly before winning the Battle of Amoltos Even in the war-torn Heartlands, set-piece battles with large armies after the fashion of the Godswar, the Tronarii conflicts, or the Khushkan war are relatively uncommon. Most combat is the result of smaller-scale engagements: raids, ambushes, banditry. No matter what kind of fighting one is doing, though, it usually takes up relatively little of a warrior's daily experience. A soldier in a mass army on campaign spends most of their time marching, making camp, or standing guard; one who spends their months clearing out bandits or the Wraith-touched still takes more time to search for their foes than to battle them. For their own part, raiders and bandits usually try to avoid fighting whenever possible, because it's bad business. In all circumstances, combat is a small, even tiny, amount of terror, shock, and death amidst a broader reality of grinding drudgery. Ambushes, skirmishes, and raids, the most common forms of combat, often involve little straight-up fighting at all — and a great deal of killing or subduing enemies through surprise. Set-piece fights with large armies are different. Thanks to the existence of shields and body armor and to the tightly packed nature of many formations, most set-piece battles result in very few casualties — at least, during the battles themselves. The two opposing forces maneuver against each other, sometimes clashing and jabbing away with their spears before separating again to lick their wounds and recover their strength, but few fighters die in the face-to-face melee. What truly determines who wins a battle is morale. As soon as enough warriors on one side take enough counsel of their fear to want to run away, that side starts to retreat whether the general wants to do so or not... and that, not the main clash of spear against spear, is usually when the slaughter begins. Unable to remain in formation, a fleeing foe is easy prey for the opposing side. As a result, the thing that generals and soldiers alike care most about is warding off terror. A mark of a truly well-trained warrior, such as a paladin of one of the divine military orders, is being able to join battle silently, without needing to pause to psychologically prepare for the clash of spears and shields. Most warriors cannot do this, and need to remind themselves that they are part of a larger whole, alongside sisters and brothers fighting for the same purpose. They sing songs to lighten their mood and subsume their own emotions into a pounding beat or a warrior's chant. Many such pieces were originally composed by valkyries, who don't need to sing them for their own good but who often lead larger allied armies of the less-professional both in battle and in music. Lest anyone get the impression that valkyries are always prim and proper, Lumia's sun warriors, who've often fought in the ranks before joining the Order of the Argent Wing, are as likely to teach their allies grimly comic or raunchy joke songs as they are hymns or wistful ballads. Anything to keep nervous allied warriors in the line alongside their comrades. This also means, though, that warriors take whatever opportunity they can to frighten their enemy. Shining, well-maintained armor and shields, gleaming weapons, a display of magical power, a host of physically unusual allies like centaurs, the gleam of valkyries' wings, a magically-amplified battle cry or grim warning from the opposing general: all can make an warrior rethink the likely outcome of a clash with such dangerous foes. Some mages even possess powers of mind to directly attack the willpower of the soldiers fighting them. It is possible, however, to take this too far, and go beyond cleverness into military uselessness. Some small professional forces have tried to demonstrate complicated formations and maneuvers as a sign of how well-drilled they are, which can frighten a less-talented foe, but if their opponents simply keep their heads and attack, the resulting confusion usually results in the collapse of the 'well-drilled' army's formation[silly|, as with the Lakedaimonians at Leuktra]. When battle is joined, it is usually for a purpose. The most obvious one is material. Just as bandits attack lone travelers to take their possessions, so too do great armies fight each other for spoils. After all, the entourage of an aristocrat from, say, Yvennes contains a great deal of plunder: the large assortment of expensive bronze weapons and gear, the food, the slaves and servants brought along with the army, the camp followers and families that can be enslaved or ransomed by the winning side, and of course plenty of the ubiquitous electrum coins. Because of this, even a dangerously well-armed aristocrat's entourage is a better target than a poor village. Looting is not merely an activity for after the battle, either. When a well-equipped warrior falls, the fighting will refocus on their body as wealthy and poor combatants alike try to seize it and strip it of its valuables. And if there are any prisoners after a battle, they are invariably ransomed or enslaved — usually the latter. One thing does often alleviate casualties, and has become somewhat more common since the Godswar: rather than face slaughter or maiming in the pursuit after a lost battle, many defeated foes are willing (or downright excited) to offer up their bodies in exchange for their lives. As far as the undisciplined and brutish are concerned, a foe in one's power is better used for baser purposes anyway, and besides, killing is usually a worst-choice in the lean years following the apocalypse. The orcs of the Sailgraves are the most notorious practitioners of this right of conquest, but even if otherwise uncommon, the possibility of less-than-lethal combat ending with sexual gratification and either an assertion of dominance or enslavement is at least known and understood by anyone in Savarra who takes part in battle — when it is not the explicit reason for battle, which it may well be. Not all combat is about loot or l[silly|ewds|ust], of course. There are battles of conquest, fought to seize territory and subjects, which were uncommon in the immediate aftermath of the Godswar but now occur more and more frequently as the Heartlands' wealth in productive land and people grows. There are battles fought against the Wraith-touched, to defend lives against the soulless monsters that continue to lurk in the shadows. Finally, of course, there are battles between groups of the living who fight simply because they hate each other, where plunder and even conquest are secondary conditions. Plunder, honor, hunger, hatred, justice, fame: all are good enough to get ordinary soldiers to march into battle. But once they're in the thick of the fighting, things become different, and men and women seize on different reasons to avoid running away from the spear-points in front of them. More than a few stand fast for the sake of those next to them, to avoid letting them down. Others, especially in mass armies, fight because they have little choice, because the densely packed infantry formations box them in and make flight impossible. Last, but not least, there are those rare professionals whose greatest bulwark against terror is that they have simply been doing this for a long time, they are good at it, and they have a pride of craft and skill that keeps them from fleeing like woodcocks.
rows.translation: ——安提戈涅，这位经验丰富的贝尔哈兰银盾军团的将军，在赢得阿莫尔托斯战役之前，正在激励自己的部队。 即便是在这个饱受战争摧残的腹地，那种像神战、特洛纳里族冲突或库什坎战争那样，动用大规模军队的正规战役也相对少见。大多数战斗实际上都是小规模冲突的结果：袭击、伏击、抢劫……无论情况如何都是如此。善良尽管进行战斗是战士日常任务的重要组成部分，但实际上，战斗通常只占他们日常活动的很小一部分。在大规模军队中作战的士兵，大部分时间都在行军、扎营或站岗；而那些需要花费数月时间来消灭土匪或那些受到邪恶力量影响的敌人的战士，他们用来寻找对手的时间，其实比真正与他们交战的时间还要长。对于劫掠者和强盗来说，他们通常会尽量避免战斗，因为这样做并不符合他们的利益。在任何情况下，战斗都只会在那种枯燥乏味的劳作生活中带来短暂的恐惧、震惊和死亡。 埋伏、小规模战斗和突袭是最常见的战斗形式，这些战斗往往几乎不涉及正面的直接交锋，而是通过突然袭击来消灭或制服敌人。而那些需要动用大规模军队的正规战役则有所不同。得益于盾牌和护甲的存在，以及许多战斗阵型的紧密排列，大多数固定场景下的战斗造成的伤亡都非常少——至少在战斗进行的过程中是这样。两支对立的军队会互相调动战术，有时会用长矛进行交锋和刺击，然后又分开来休整伤口、恢复体力，但在面对面的近战中，很少有战士会丧生。真正决定一场战斗胜负的因素是士气。一旦某一方有足够多的战士被恐惧所驱使，想要逃跑，那么无论指挥官是否愿意，那一方就会开始撤退……而恰恰是在这种时候，而不是在刀枪交锋的正面上，杀戮才会真正开始。一旦无法保持队形，逃跑的敌人就很容易成为对方的猎物。 因此，对于将领和士兵来说，最关心的事情就是如何抵御恐怖。而一个真正训练有素的战士——比如那些属于神圣军事组织的圣骑士——的标志，就是能够在战斗中保持冷静，无需停下来进行心理准备，就能直接投入战斗。大多数战士都无法做到这一点，他们需要时刻提醒自己：自己其实是某个更大整体的一部分，与那些为共同目标而战的兄弟姐妹们紧密相连。他们会通过歌唱来缓解情绪，将自己的情感融入那强劲的节奏或战士们的呼喊之中。许多这样的曲目最初都是由女武神创作的。对于她们来说，演唱这些歌曲并非出于个人需求，而是常常在战斗与音乐领域中带领那些不太专业的盟军部队。为了避免有人误以为女武神总是端庄得体，卢米娅那些曾在战场上浴血奋战后才加入银翼骑士团的太阳战士们，同样会向他们的盟友传授一些既滑稽又粗俗的笑话歌曲，而也会演唱赞美诗或充满怀旧的民谣。任何能够让紧张的盟军战士们与他们的战友们一起坚守阵地的手段都值得采用。 这也意味着，战士们会利用一切机会来恐吓他们的敌人。闪亮的、保养良好的盔甲和盾牌、光芒四射的武器、魔法的展示、半人马这样的特殊盟友、女武神的羽翼所散发出的光芒、经过魔法增幅的战斗口号，或是敌方将领发出的严厉警告——所有这些因素都可能让战士重新考虑与如此危险的敌人交战的结果。有些法师甚至拥有精神力量，能够直接攻击与他们交战的士兵的意志力。然而，如果将这种能力运用得过于极端，就会从巧妙战术转变为毫无军事意义的举动。有些小型专业部队曾试图通过展示复杂的队形和战术动作来证明他们的训练有素，这种做法确实可能吓退能力较弱的对手，但倘若对方的战士们能够保持冷静并发起攻击，这种混乱局面通常会导致那些“训练有素”的军队阵型瓦解。[silly|就像在勒乌克特拉战役中拉科代蒙人所做的那样。]当战斗爆发时，通常都是有着某种目的的。最显而易见的目的就是争夺财物。就像强盗会袭击独行的旅人以抢夺他们的财物一样，强大的军队之间争斗也是为了抢夺战利品。毕竟，比如说来自伊文尼斯的贵族随从们会携带大量的战利品：各种昂贵的青铜武器和装备、食物、随军而来的奴隶与仆从，还有那些可以被获胜一方奴役或赎买的随军家属，当然，还有大量随处可见的琥珀金币。正因如此，即便是那些武装精良的贵族随从，也比一个贫穷的村庄更容易成为攻击目标。抢劫也并非只在战斗结束后才会发生。当一名装备精良的战士倒下时，战斗的焦点就会立刻转移到他的身上——无论是富人还是穷人，都会争相抢夺他的财物。而在战斗之后，如果有俘虏被俘，他们通常会被赎走或者沦为奴隶——后者居多。 有一件事确实能够在很大程度上减少人员伤亡，而且自从“神战”之后，这种情况变得愈发普遍：在一场失败的战斗之后，许多被击败的敌人都愿意（甚至可以说是兴高采烈地）用自己的生命来换取自己的性命，从而避免被屠杀或致残。对于那些缺乏纪律、行为野蛮的人来说，手握强权时，利用敌人来满足低级欲望倒也是个不错的选择。更何况，在末日之后的艰难时期，杀戮通常并不是最好的选择。帆葬群岛族的兽人正是这种征服行为的典型代表，但即便这种行为并不常见，任何参与战斗的萨瓦拉人至少也都了解：在非致命的战斗中，通过性行为来确立支配地位或使敌人沦为奴隶，也是完全有可能发生的事情——甚至有时候，这本身就是战斗的直接目的。为了战斗，很可能确实如此。 并非所有战斗都只为战利品或[silly|淫事|色欲]，当然。有些战役是为了争夺领土和臣民而进行的，这种战斗在“神战”结束后并不常见，但随着腹地拥有更多的肥沃土地和人口，这类战役如今变得越来越频繁了。人们为了保护人类的生命，与那些被怨灵侵蚀的怪物展开了激战，这些无魂的怪物依然潜伏在阴影之中。当然，也存在着一些生者之间的战斗——这些冲突仅仅源于彼此之间的仇恨，而在这些战斗中，掠夺甚至征服都只是次要的目的。 掠夺、荣誉、饥饿、仇恨、正义、名声：这些因素都足以激励普通士兵奔赴战场。但一旦他们陷入激烈的战斗之中，情况就会发生变化，男男女女都会找各种借口来逃避前方的刀光剑影。有不少人为了身边的人而坚持到底，不愿让他们失望。而另一些人，尤其是在大规模军队中，之所以战斗，是因为他们别无选择——因为密集的步兵阵型将他们困住，使得逃跑变得不可能。最后但同样重要的是，还有一些罕见的专业人士，他们抵御恐怖主义的最大武器就是：他们已经从事这一工作很长时间了，他们非常擅长这份工作，而且他们对自己的技艺充满自豪感，这种自豪感使他们不会像山鹑一样惊慌逃窜。

rows.translation: 继续挖那条沟。挖完之后，再挖一条。

—Emperor Edivus II to his soldiers, shortly before the siege defense of Marouka
        
        The Belharans built many walled places around their empire, the remnants of a crash fortification program in the midst of the Godswar. It had mixed results during the war itself, but some of the mighty Belharan mural barriers do still stand around and inside Heartlander cities. Other fortified places remain empty, or have been occupied by bandits in the intervening centuries. For these fortifications, the imperials built monumental stone walls, often using blocks cut and fitted together by magic. Modern cities sometimes add onto the extant Belharan fortifications when necessary, but often let them slowly crumble away (or raid them for stone to build other things). It's not usually engineering knowledge that the builders of today lack, save perhaps a few of the more arcane spells and advanced math, but rather labor and resources. Under such constraints, a quick patch job, a wooden palisade, and a ditch are more than sufficient for most defenders' needs.[silly| Small chance of any academics wandering in to hector Savarrans about where their ditch is!]

        Ditches, walls, and other fortifications mean that armies rarely assault fortified places if they can avoid it. Few realms have the sort of resources to sustain a real army, let alone a proper engineering corps for their army to overcome such defenses. However, for those that do, like Khor'minos, attacking a walled fortification usually boils down to building a large berm, or mole, of compacted earth that fills in any ditches in front of a wall and reaches high enough to allow archers and mages to scale the mole and fire down on the defenders of a wall. After they clear the wall, it becomes safe enough for infantry to scale it with ladders and capture it. Of course, if there is anyone in the assaulting army who can fly above the fortifications, the task of clearing the wall becomes much simpler — another reason why Lumia's valkyries and Sorra's harpies are highly prized warriors in serious conflicts.
        
        It is known that the ancients sometimes had other means of breaking into cities. They had some siege engines, although those few that survive mostly seem to have been used to clear warriors off of the tops of walls rather than breaking the walls themselves. Magic is also a possibility, but few spells have the sort of concussive power needed to seriously damage stone, brick, or earth fortifications. There are also literary references to undermining walls with tunnels so that they collapse, but in the modern era, few can manage such a feat save the myrmarcs of southern Belhar and the Minoans... and these masters of engineering do not share their secrets lightly.
        
        Defenders, of course, have their own countermeasures. They can generally collect more food than their besiegers can, and have the advantage of fortifications to base their fight around. It may take quite a long time for an attacking army to even reach the main walls of a city, let alone overcome them and breach them, and they will be subject to sallying raids by the defenders at every step. The defenders have, in fact, so many advantages that apart from the valkyries and harpies and the legendary engineering prowess of Khor'minos, few in Savarra can reliably assault well-defended stone fortifications. As a result, most such places, if they fall at all, fall to treachery or sneak attacks, or simply negotiate terms with their attackers to avoid the hassle of a siege. A successful propaganda program can be critical to making the last solution viable; the Minoans, for example, often host envoys from foreign powers in chambers decorated with reliefs of the legions assaulting cities, an unsubtle reminder of what they can do better than most.
rows.translation:
——埃迪瓦斯二世在马鲁卡防御战前夕对士兵们说道：
        
        贝拉尔人他们在自己的帝国内建造了许多设防城市，这些都是在“神战”期间匆忙修建的防御工事的遗迹。在战争期间，这些防御工事取得的成效参差不齐，但如今，一些强大的贝尔哈兰壁画屏障依然矗立在赫特兰德的城市之中。而其他一些设防地点要么依然空置着，要么在几个世纪以来被强盗们占据了。为了建造这些防御工事，帝国人们修建了巨大的石墙，这些石块往往是通过魔法切割并拼接而成的。现代城市在必要时也会对现存的贝尔哈兰防御工事进行扩建，但通常会任由其逐渐毁坏（或者拆取其石料来建造其他建筑）。如今，建造者们所缺乏的通常并不是工程知识——也许除了那些较为深奥的咒语和高级数学知识之外——而是劳动力与资源。在这种限制条件下，对于大多数防御者来说，简单的修补工作、木制栅栏以及一道壕沟就已经足够满足他们的需求了。[silly| 有没有学者会偶然走进来，质问赫克托·萨瓦兰他们的沟渠到底在哪儿呢？]

        壕沟、城墙以及其他防御工事意味着，如果可以避免的话，军队很少会进攻设有这些防御设施的地方。几乎没有哪个王国拥有足够的资源来维持一支真正的军队，更不用说拥有一支能够攻克这类防御工事的工程部队了。然而，对于那些采用这种策略的势力来说，比如科尔米诺斯，攻击有围墙的防御工事通常意味着要建造一道由压实的泥土构成的高墙——这道墙可以填平城墙前的所有壕沟，其高度也足以让弓箭手和法师攀爬上去，向城墙内的守军发起攻击。当他们清除了那道墙后，阵地就变得足够安全了，步兵们可以借助梯子攀上墙去占领它。当然，如果进攻军队中有人能够飞越那些防御工事，那么清除那道墙的任务就会变得容易得多——这也是为什么在激烈的战斗中，卢米娅的女武神们和索拉的鹰身女妖们会被视为极其珍贵的战士。
        
        众所周知，古代人们有时会使用其他方法来攻破城市。他们拥有一些攻城器械，不过那些现存下来的器械似乎大多被用来清除城墙顶部的守军，而不是用来直接破坏城墙本身。魔法也是一种可能性，但很少有法术具备足以严重破坏石制、砖制或土制防御工事的破坏力。虽然也有文献记载过通过挖掘隧道来削弱城墙使其倒塌的策略，但在现代，除了贝尔哈尔南部的蚁族和米诺斯人之外，几乎没有人能够做到这一点。而这些工程大师们，是不会轻易透露他们的秘密的。
        
        防御者当然也有自己的应对措施。他们通常能够收集到比进攻者更多的食物，而且还有防御工事的掩护，可以以此为基础展开战斗。对于进攻军队来说，要攻打到城市的主体城墙可能需要相当长的时间，更不用说攻破它们了。在每一步前进的过程中，他们都会遭到防御者的出击和骚扰。事实上，防御方拥有太多优势，以至于除了那些女武神、鹰身女妖，以及科尔米诺斯那举世闻名的工程技术之外，萨瓦拉地区几乎没有人能够有效地攻破那些防御严密的石制要塞。因此，这类地方之所以会沦陷，往往是因为背叛、偷袭，或者仅仅是防御方与进攻方达成了某种协议，从而避免了围攻带来的麻烦。一个成功的宣传计划对于使最后的解决方案具有可行性而言至关重要。例如，米诺斯人常常让外国使节们进入那些装饰着描绘军队攻城场景的浮雕的房间，这种做法无疑是在向人们强调：他们在某些方面确实比大多数国家更出色。

rows.original: "But what is most incredible of all is that in journeying beyond these mountains, they arrived very near to the surface of the Moon, a shining land ruled by Tira herself, and saw many things which must be supposed by others to be exaggerated inventions."
rows.translation: 但最令人难以置信的是，在穿越这些山脉之后，他们竟然来到了距离月球表面非常近的地方——那是一片被蒂拉亲自统治的、光芒闪耀的土地。在那里，他们看到了许多事物，而这些事物在别人看来，肯定只是被夸大其词的虚构故事罢了。
rows.raw: '\n        "But what is most incredible of all is that in journeying beyond these mountains, they arrived very near to the surface of the Moon, a shining land ruled by Tira herself, and saw many things which must be supposed by others to be exaggerated inventions."\n        '

rows.original: —The Wonders Beyond the Sands, composed many centuries before the Godswar by an unknown Belharan author Old Belhar conquered most of the world before the outbreak of the Godswar. It sent fleets and armies to strange lands that had seemed mystical and mysterious to those who lived in the Heartlands, and although its rule over some of them, like Jassira and Tronarii, lasted long enough for them to remain integrated into the Belharan world system even after the empire dissolved, others remain nearly as mysterious as they were before the Belharan invasion... if not more so. Even the croc-folk and anubians who ply the inland rivers and deserts of Jassira cannot manage to cross the vast sea of dunes that stretches beyond the sultanate's borders. No oases can be found, no safe route devised, no caravans organized to try to reach whatever lies beyond — if anything does. Yet, from time to time, in the suqs of [silly|Krokodeilopolis|Crocodopolis] and the open-air markets of the sultana's mountainous province of Arkacia, blue stones of tremendous beauty and worth appear for sale, sometimes in well-crafted jewelry and sometimes in the raw, with flecks of gold shining out from their oceanic depths. Such stones work better than nearly any other as magical catalysts, and with this use and its beautiful deep-blue coloration in mind, the Jassirans named them azul. Their name has stuck. Belharan geographers knew nothing of whence it came, but hypothesized a "foreign land" and named it, with no sense of irony, Xenaspa. This was the land beyond the desert, and legends of it grew with every fresh sample of azul jewelry that mysteriously appeared. Only in the era of Belharan conquest did people learn some of the truth behind the stories of Xenaspa. Beyond the sands there truly were populous, wealthy realms, though the deserts and mountains between them and Jassira were so imposing that the Belharans only found them by sailing around the mountains entirely, through treacherous waters and against difficult currents, aided by powerful magics. Most of the details of the lands they found are lost, but what is known is that the lockstep legions triumphed in many battles over the peoples who lived there in "the land of a thousand cities" — some of which were of the races that remain familiar to Belharans from their home continent, and others of decidedly new ones. When it was done, they had conquered a vast new imperial province bearing the name Xenaspa after the legendary realm. Heartlanders came to live there to govern and garrison it, intensify cultivation, extract what wealth came from it, and bring a flavor of imperial culture and religion; by all appearances, within a century Xenaspa was a relatively stable and well-integrated part of the imperial realm, even if all travel remained by sea
rows.translation: —《沙海彼端的奇观》，一位佚名贝尔哈兰作家于诸神之战前数世纪所著 诸神之战爆发以前，古贝尔哈已经征服了世界大部分地区。它向种种异域派出舰队与军团；在腹地居民眼中，那些土地神秘而不可思议。贝尔哈对其中一些地区——例如贾西拉和特洛纳里——的统治足够长久，以至帝国解体之后，它们仍融入贝尔哈世界体系；另一些地方却依然像贝尔哈入侵前一样神秘……甚至更加神秘。 即使是往来于贾西拉内陆河流与沙漠的鳄鱼人和阿努比斯人，也无法跨越苏丹国边界之外的浩瀚沙海。那里找不到绿洲，规划不出安全路线，也组织不起商队去尝试抵达彼端之物——假如彼端真有什么的话。然而，[silly|克罗科代洛波利斯|鳄鱼城]的露天市集与苏丹娜治下阿尔卡西亚山地行省的集市中，偶尔会出现价值惊人、无比美丽的蓝色宝石。有些被制成精巧首饰，有些则保持原石形态；金色斑点从海洋般深邃的蓝色中熠熠闪光。这种石头用作魔法触媒时几乎胜过所有其他材料。贾西拉人因其用途与美丽的深蓝色泽，将它命名为“阿祖尔”，这一名称也沿用至今。贝尔哈地理学家不知道宝石来自哪里，只能假设存在一片“异邦”，还毫无讽刺意味地将其命名为“塞纳斯帕”。那便是沙漠彼端的土地；每当新一批阿祖尔首饰神秘现世，关于它的传说便更加繁盛。 直到贝尔哈征服时代，人们才了解到塞纳斯帕传说背后的部分真相。沙海彼端确实存在人口稠密、富庶繁荣的国度，但它们与贾西拉之间的沙漠和群山实在险峻，贝尔哈人只能借助强大魔法，绕过整片山脉，在危险海域与艰难洋流中航行，最终才找到它们。关于那些土地的大部分细节都已失传；只知道纪律严整的军团曾在“千城之地”与当地族群多次交战并取得胜利。当地有些种族仍与贝尔哈人在故乡大陆熟悉的族群相同，另一些则截然陌生。战事结束后，他们征服了一片广阔的新行省，并以传说中的国度为其命名“塞纳斯帕”。腹地人移居当地，负责治理与驻防、扩大耕作、攫取财富，并带去帝国文化与宗教。种种迹象表明，不出一个世纪，塞纳斯帕便已成为帝国领土中相对稳定且高度融合的一部分，尽管所有往来仍只能依靠海路
